projects.notes: Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them.

projects.notes: 2026-11-09/10: Octatrack beta: the silence after USB DISK MODE (finding 72) was the base mistaking stock's DSP pause for a stall, fixed (I69); FM Synth with many FLEX tracks no longer loses the audio on PLAY; the Octatrack page asks for a power cycle when the DSP has stopped; Temp Save 0.1.0 withdrawn from USB installs (card build stays). Modwerk also loads effects onto Zoom MultiStomp pedals now (ZDL files over USB; not an Elektron device). Browser-based hub, builds locally from the user's own stock OS. Browse mods by device, forum with a section per device, shared SDK. Dubspot (13 Oct): several modules are still early prototypes. last_activity = date of the Dubspot article, not a forum post. 2026-11-02: three Analog Rytm MKII modules by npp1993 moved into the library (Pipo Loop 0.1.1, Sample RATE 0.1.0, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.6.0, all experimental, OS 1.74; linkable together with core-ar2 0.7, Filter Hz and Loop Sync; the packages themselves not yet run on a unit). `_submissions/` takes no new modules. The Octatrack USB beta also works on the MKI. 2026-11-03: the site now lets you download a built Analog Rytm MKII .syx (after confirming you know how to get back to stock); new Rytm module quick-velocity-aftertouch-assign with a verification note. Zoom pedals: an effect whose group+ID clashes with one already on the pedal is moved to a free local Delay ID 958-1023 (ID only in the ZDL header at 0x40-0x41, no checksum); two effects with the same group and ID froze an MS-70CDR at boot until its ROM was reprogrammed. 2026-11-04/05: Rytm MKII downloads on (records); npp1993's Control In Actions (footswitch or 0-5 V gate on EXP/CV IN as ACTION for MUTE and more) and Quick Velocity+Aftertouch Assign join the library, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.7.0; euclidean 1.1.6 for Digitakt I 1.53/1.54 reported working on a unit by sumedho (all cases, save/reload, power cycle). 2026-11-08 to 11-10 (74c9eb2): Rytm library gains comp-preview, kit-ab, lfo-rnd and voice-dac (from rytm2_mods, unit runs on the Modwerk base), ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes (from rytm-mods-src 0017/0018, unit runs T208/T210/T221), Improved Machine Browser and MIDI Mute; the Octatrack key bus moved to the tail of the first FX2 slot (checked on an MKI and an MKII); a Digitakt II audio scheduler is proposed (emulator only); Zoom MS-70CDR pedal work (out of scope here).

projects.notes: Windows standalone builder (portable, no Python/Git/WSL needed) that takes the user's own official OS file, identifies it by SHA-256, writes the patched .syx; the user installs it with Elektron Transfer. The builder never connects to the instrument and never flashes. Adds two random-loop LFO waveforms on all three LFOs: DV-F (WAVE 7, free-running) and DV-T (WAVE 8, read position resets on track trigger); MODE = 2/4/8/16/32 steps; SPH = randomness (0 new values each step, 64 locks values and order, 127 keeps values but reorders, in between blends); stock WAVE 0-6 stay on stock paths. v0.2.0-beta adds a ONESHOT waveform zoom (encoder C cycles 1x, 2x, 3.75x, turning C pans; only in the combined 1.17 edition). Hardware: all three outputs validated on a physical unit for normal boot and operation, described by the author as beta evidence, not exhaustive. Open: broad MIDI / sequencer / transport / sync regression, save-reload-power-cycle persistence, long-duration stability. Unsigned .exe (SmartScreen warns). Repo: docs/INSTALLATION.md and docs/RECOVERY.md, windows-builder/, src/dv/ (host model), coldfire/ (DV, routing, trampoline, startup-allocation source), research/ (byte-backed findings), tools/midisniff.py (passive SysEx capture, does not transmit). Evidence ladder used by the author: SOURCE/STATIC, HOST, SYNTHETIC UNICORN, NATURAL EMULATED, HARDWARE. MIT, 7 commits, 4 stars. Credits: Marbles (concept only), Bezronczek's Syntakt Firmware Workbench (behavioural reference), ElekLabs digikit (research tooling, not bundled), elektron-firmware-tool (vendored). 2026-11-06: a second package, the Digitakt II Sample Editing Pack (OS 1.17, Windows builder): Universal Zoom (up to 64x), SmartSlice (automatic slice points), SampleLAB (load or record, chop, trim, audition, save copies) and CFADE (cross-fade at the SLICE loop wrap). Derived from digikit, AGPL-3.0-or-later; hardware acceptance by the author recorded in sample-editing/HARDWARE_ACCEPTANCE.md (user report, not an agent-run test).

projects.base_os: Digitone II OS 1.12 only (patcher refuses any other file); NOT compatible with dn2mk2 (OS 1.11)
projects.version: v1.3 (2026-11-04): per-sound LFOs, two envelope followers and two arps as modulators (played on a Digitone II per README); v1.2 (2026-10-30): instant pattern switch (PTN + YES/NO), saved with the project; v1.1 (2026-10-30) GROOVE rework and tap tempo; v1.0.1 (2026-10-29) fixes OS installs over Transfer while Overtone runs
projects.notes: Python 3.11+ patcher (patcher/patch.py) that builds Overtone from the user's own OS 1.12 and only saves the result if it matches the tested build byte for byte; install via Elektron Transfer over USB. Adds machines SOPHIE, MACHINEDRUM, LOOP, THRU, per-track insert effects, envelope followers, two arpeggiators, parameter slides and GROOVE (replaces swing). 1.0.1 fixes installing an OS sent with Transfer while Overtone runs. About 160 checks per build in two emulators (digikit for the main OS, a SHARC emulator for the DSP program); author states 1.0.1 passes all of them, is played on a Digitone II and Transfer installs were checked on the unit. Opening Overtone projects on stock OS is untested. Recovery section is detailed (FUNC + TRIG 4, DIN MIDI, ~15 min). AGPL-3.0-or-later (includes dnfw), 5 commits. Related: dnfw, digikit, dn2-cfw, Schwung Sophie (MIT), and the author's digitone-2-modding-skill used with Claude Code.

projects.name: SYXGRID v2
projects.author: xrcstrecords
projects.notes: Free browser-based pattern/sequence editor, not a firmware mod. Repo includes sysexmap/, a public reverse-engineered SysEx format map (CC BY 4.0): 45 mappings, map version 1.13.0, each with a confidence level (A = hardware-confirmed on a DN2: 23; B = corpus-confirmed by repo fixtures: 12; C = inherited, one value exercised: 9; D = unknown, do not rely: 1). Narrowed by bisection on 2026-09-08 against a Digitone II (OS 1.10E) and a Digitakt II. Not decoded: parameter locks, sound parameters (filter, amp, FX, LFO), synth machine choice. Needs the DN2 in SYSEX RECEIVE mode; Web MIDI needs Chromium over HTTPS or localhost (Chrome/Edge 152 break SysEx receive on macOS). App is AGPLv3 since v22.46 (MIT through v22.37). 6 commits.

projects.name: DN2 DT2 firmware research
projects.author: armio
projects.base_os: Digitone II OS 1.11 (target) + Digitakt II OS 1.16 (donor); both official files supplied locally
projects.version: R022 candidate (2026-11-06): working-project sample autosave and sampler SYN-page routing fixes; native replay passed, hardware confirmation pending; includes R020 cold-start guard and R013 FORMAT SAMPLES; an iPhone USB freeze is unresolved; R012 remains the stable target
projects.tested_note: README: R012 confirmed on hardware; R021 and R022 hardware confirmation pending (read 2026-11-11)
projects.notes: Source-only recipes for Digitone II firmware with six Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE), stereo samples, sample browsing, DT2 parameter graphics and SLICES trig mode. Recorder adds recording/resampling, source selection, normalization, trimming, audition, saving to +Drive and optional track assignment; VOICE cycles Voice Setup, Sample Manager and Recorder. Class-compliant USB audio provides 42 capture channels at 48 kHz/24 bit (MAIN, tracks 1-16, DELAY, REVERB, CHORUS, INPUT as stereo pairs) and a stereo return. R012 needs only the official DN2 1.11 and DT2 1.16 OS files; silent compatibility data replaces the private sample bank, and users load their own playable samples afterward. Native and browser builders verify exact inputs and the output: 2,563,872 bytes, SHA-256 4a2742a4...63a3a9a. The browser builds locally without uploading files; neither builder flashes the instrument. No firmware images or samples are distributed. Historical exact T1E2/R003/R008/R011 builds still require their original private sample bank. R011 fixed USB publication stalling after project changes by selecting its candidate destination from current DMA START while preserving ownership checks; R012 retains that fix. Owner-confirmed stock audio, samples, Recorder and USB audio on R012, including after project changes. Stable does not mean exhaustive validation: exact trimmed-file comparison, full Recorder-source coverage, endurance and end-to-end USB latency remain unverified. Builds on dnfw (angellinares/dn2_firmware_explore), selache, digikit and elektron-firmware-tool. AGPL-3.0-or-later. 2026-11-03: README warns new users NOT to install R012 yet. R012 mounts an existing sample filesystem but does not create one on a DN2 that never had it; symptoms are 0% Free / 0 bytes in Transfer, stalled uploads, Connection failed. The author says stock FORMAT +DRIVE, EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET do not create it and can erase projects; at that point an on-device formatter was still in development. R013 subsequently added FORMAT SAMPLES with erase confirmation; formatting, restart, capacity and post-format uploads were checked on the owner's unit. Owner testing of R012 had used storage prepared during development. An earlier track-2 saved-project reload report was an unsaved checkpoint; R022 addresses a separate, reproduced failure to refresh the sample table in the unsaved working-state backup. This does not establish recovery from an interrupted write or USB freeze.

projects.tested_note: README (2026-11-10): digikit has run on a real Digitakt II (OS 1.17: runtime, PLUCK, bootscreen per finding 117); the Digitone II only in the emulator; Frequency shifter, Overdrive curves and TB303 emulator only. 2026-11-11: Fast USB (a vendor bulk interface) ran on a Digitone II (OS 1.12) and a Digitakt II (OS 1.17) after a fix found on the DN2 (I70)

projects.notes: Native Rust emulator that runs the ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together, with front panel, display and audio, plus a web panel (WASM core), a Tauri desktop app, the patch toolchain "patchkit" (applies modules to the user's own .syx), a headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes, a control socket for patch injection and DSP/ColdFire analysis databases with Ghidra tooling. README caveats: the DSP "does not run in real time yet", the browser host is parked on branch wip/browser-host, "no patched firmware has been installed on a device", and recovery via the bootstrap menu is "not tested on hardware". patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8. 982 commits, AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra section-7 terms (attribution, origin, names) in NOTICE; page shows 46 open issues. GitHub marks it as not a fork. The org ElekLabs has 2 public repos: digikit and a fork of js216/selache. Original author: the GitHub profile m-dwyer is named "Em D" (Melbourne), which is exactly the credit ElekLabs' NOTICE requires ("digikit by Em D"); Overtone credits digikit to "Em D" as well. The earlier repo m-dwyer/digikit (196 commits, 4 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later, README at the time: "no audio", last visible file HANDOVER-2026-09-16) shows no move/archive notice and does not mention ElekLabs. ElekLabs has no public members, so the pages themselves do not show who runs it; the maintainer (user of this repo) states that Em D develops in ElekLabs/digikit (2026-10-31, not verifiable on the pages). The licence changed from GPL-2.0-or-later to AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra terms. Treat both repos as one project line, ElekLabs/digikit being the current one. Mod READMEs that say "digikit's emulator" mean this project.

projects.author: gdeo607

projects.notes: Base mod for gdeo607's Digitakt II machine mods; on its own it changes nothing. It keeps irpina's core 1.0 hook bus and adds digikit's machine, parameter and DSP-inline frameworks as core services: added machine types 7-23 and parameter codes 275-338, DSP voices as relocatable objects placed in free DSP L2, a second SRC page with four saved, p-lockable controls (stored in the sound record's spare slots 77 and 78; such projects still load on the stock OS), and since 2.6 a pattern service that reads and edits trigs and locks through the firmware's own editors. Building needs an elekloader with `sharc_raw` support for the Digitakt II (a branch of gdeo607's elekloader fork, proposed upstream). Do not flash 2.4, 2.5 or 2.6: they crash the unit at boot (I67).

Gate: CLEARED TO FLASH.
projects.tested_note: gated in the emulator (v0.48 adds a first gate step with ColdFire and DSP emulated together); units ran v0.44-v0.47: v0.44 froze (I65), BOUNCE recorded nothing or never played back (I66), a user's v0.47 dropped a sample voice block by block under load (I71); v0.48's fine controls are not verified on hardware (FIRMWARE.md)
projects.notes: Adds Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE) with sample browser and recorder, PERC (34 Machinedrum machines incl. TRX, EFM, GND, P-I), Monomachine voices (SID 6581, DPRO WAVE/DDRW/DENS, VO-6) and a CPU guard. Browser-based patcher builds from the user's own files ("nothing is uploaded") and saves only if the output sha256 matches a build that passed scripts/ship_gate.py. Hardware: README says verification is pending per version; FIRMWARE.md says nearly every v0.21-v0.33 entry was checked in emulators and "not seen on hardware yet". Main open problem: DSP time (heavy voices cut sound). Flashing a 1.12 unit takes it back to a 1.11 base, projects saved under the newer OS may not open. 1,491 commits, 8 stars, AGPL-3.0-or-later. FIRMWARE.md says built firmware is kept on the repo's `builds` branch (not main) - unlike most projects here, which only ship patchers; we link only to the repo and docs, not to builds. Withdrawn builds: v0.4-v0.7 (oversized image). v0.38 (2026-11-02): Direct Jump state kept in its own +Drive sector (0x6FF000); per-project sample lists at +Drive 0x6D0000-0x6E02FF, two checked copies each. Root cause of the silent new samples: the DSP plays a pool slot only below the directory's count, and live adds did not update the count. v0.39 (2026-11-03): recordings had kept only ~2 ms since v0.38 because the DSP recorder took words 2-4 of every new link command as source, channel and threshold, and v0.38 sent a check command at every take's start; now only the recorder's own commands set them.

projects.name: digitone-2-modding-skill

projects.notes: Agent skill (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor; install with `npx skills add`) for developing Digitone II firmware mods: ColdFire MAIN OS patching in C, SHARC DSP audio code, verification in two emulators (digikit + a whole-DSP SHARC emulator), rebuild/re-sign/flash over USB. Encodes stock-firmware addresses, hook sites, the ColdFire-to-DSP frame format, free memory and "hardware rules the emulators cannot check, which each once silenced a real unit" - read on 2026-10-31 via SKILL.md and references/*.md (SKILL.md has 20 rules incl. whole 32-byte boot blocks, stock encodings only, no L2 above 0x200B0000, never read unwritten DDR, 2 MiB image / section 7 under 1 MiB, stop after two failed flashes; scripts include hwrules.py, shapecheck.py, encodecheck.py, bootblocks.py, sim.py/simc.py, cfmod.py, rpc_flash.py). Facts and rules are folded into hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md and hardware/common/agent-workflow.md. Note: tree pages are blocked for our fetcher by robots.txt; the blob pages were readable. Examples: double_time (sequencer clock hook), track_trim (-6 dB on track 1). Needs Python 3.11+, dnfw, m68k GCC, digikit. MIT (digikit-derived files GPL-2.0), 2 commits, 10 stars. Overtone was built with it. Closest existing relative of this repo's hardware/ folder.

projects.notes: Native Rust desktop sequencer for Digitakt II, Digitone II and Analog Four, built from digi-roll. Writes to hardware: README recommends throwaway projects. Safe-write ceremony of five rules (re-read and back up the destination pattern first, OS build on an allowlist, user confirmation, change only needed bytes, read back and byte-compare). Gen-2 dump protocol (digis) vs gen-1 (Analog Four). +Drive file-write commands 0x57/0x58/0x59 hardware-verified for a single chunk only, not called by the app (writes above 16 KiB refused); 0x5A/0x5B/0x5C (move/copy/delete) not implemented. Protocol code ported from elk-herd (BSD-2, (c) mzero). Fixtures: 34 real .syx dumps. 124 commits, GPL-3.0-or-later. Not firmware modding. Windows/Linux write testing incomplete.

The GitHub page is a stub: README says the project has migrated away from GitHub to an obfuscated address (not decoded by us) and that issues and pull requests generated by AI will be summarily rejected - do not open AI-generated ones. Each mods/<name>/patch.json lists the patch location, a hash of the expected original bytes and the new bytes; tools/build/build.py refuses the wrong OS, overlapping patches and protected sections. tools/emu is a ColdFire emulator (Unicorn + EMAC model); every mod is tested there before flashing. A git hook (tools/hooks) blocks firmware files from commits - a practice worth copying. README: seven mods running on real hardware (v0.8.0); RECOVERY.md exists. Planned: PIN lock, new LFO shapes, 3rd LFO/mod matrix, arpeggiator, resampling, new machines (RISER/DOWNFILTER, SY SWARM+), web builder. MIT, 66 commits, 9 stars. Brick-risk flag set on altstrument. projects.notes: Browser tools (Web MIDI, Chromium only, nothing uploaded) for Digitone and Digitone II projects: Expander (each sound-locked Digitone 1 sound gets its own track on the Digitone II), Manager (move/copy/swap/clear/rename patterns across banks with undo; Insights: polymeter, PATTERN RESET cost, voice use), Library (browse/search/rename the 2,048 +Drive presets; wavetables need Digitone II with "Waverider" firmware), Backup (whole +Drive into one .dnx with a manifest; excludes global settings), Probe (read-only identification and traffic capture) and CLI commands (project, plan, convert, copy, rearrange, rename, track, rebuild, diff, sheet; dry run by default). Formats: .dnprj (DN1) and .dn2prj (DN2) projects, sound banks .syx; payloads LZ4-compressed inside a ZIP; SysEx uses 8-in-7 MSB-first. Author discloses LLM use; AGPL-3.0-or-later, TypeScript, 15 stars, created 2026-09-07. Not firmware modding. projects.base_os: MDX 2.0 USR machines (Machinedrum MKI and MKII)
projects.notes: Tools around the MDS specification: mds_pack.py builds an MDS file from a JSON definition and assembled DSP56300 code (CLD, LOD or raw binary), mds-certifier runs a machine and stamps its cycle costs for MKII, MKI with the program in DRAM and MKI in SRAM, and mds_to_syx.py converts an MDS file to SysEx for a USR slot. A --quick mode checks default, minimum and maximum parameters over four blocks on all sixteen tracks. Needs Motorola's asm56300 (or a compatible assembler). GPL. projects.notes: Mod system for the Syntakt bringing Digitakt mk1 sample machines (ONE SHOT, WERP, REPITCH, SLICE), a per-project sample pool with long samples in slots 65-128 and a basic sample manager. Experimental. MIT. 18 stars at first sight. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-02; README start read. 2026-11-02: the GitHub repo no longer answers (deleted, renamed or private); details here are from the earlier read. 2026-11-03: the Lapin list links it as an external web app, https://synfact.app (builds custom Syntakt firmware from the user's stock OS file). 2026-11-03: the project moved to GSM1980/synfact-dev and was rebuilt on elekloader (GPL-2.0; the old release repo was MIT): a core (mods/core-st) with hook bus, UI and SETTINGS events, SMZ4 banks of machines and modules that can change without reinstalling, long-sample storage (HZFS) and a project sample pool. Mods: SP sample machines, SY FM DTONE, audio recorder, third LFO, arpeggiator, POLY, system info, sample manager. Builds change MAIN and a bounded part of AUDIO only; a recovery core that never loads the bank can replace a bank that stops the unit from starting. Also builds in the browser (synfact.app). A snapshot of the old release repo survives as nrdsrfr/synfact-release (2026-10-17). 2026-11-06: project lifecycle audit after a user report of slow project load and save; arp-st leaves default carriers absent (81 % fewer emulated instructions); RANDOMIZE pages documented. 2026-11-09: new docs SETUP, MACHINES (writing a machine), MACHINE-REFERENCE and SAFE-BOOT-SMZ4-07-16; a safe-boot trial crashed every boot until core 1.7.1 (I62); a companion window broke BASE/WDTH until 1.7.2 (I63).

projects.name: digitakt-reorder

projects.notes: Python library and job template that reorders, drops and de-duplicates the sample pool of a Digitakt project dump and remaps every kit and sample-lock reference. Works on a .syx file fetched and sent with elk-herd; no MIDI code. MIT.

projects.name: ElekPrep (elektron-sample-prep)
projects.author: luizvarela
projects.notes: Single-page browser sample prep: trims at zero crossings, converts to 48 kHz 16-bit WAV, works out loop lengths from BPM and steps; profiles for four devices (device list taken from the related ElekPrep Transfer app, not checked). No MIDI; files go to the unit through Transfer or Elektroid. MIT.

projects.name: ElekPrep Transfer
projects.author: unknown
projects.notes: Closed-source browser app that preps audio and sends it over Web MIDI SysEx to the +Drive, with Transfer and +Drive Manager views and device profiles for Digitakt II, Digitakt, Analog Rytm (MKI/MKII) and Model:Samples. Proprietary; author not named. Relation to luizvarela's ElekPrep not established (same name). Interesting as a second independent implementation of +Drive upload over SysEx.

projects.name: Digitone 2 Pattern Manager
projects.author: morukutsu
projects.notes: Closed-source browser app: requests Pattern+Kit dumps from a Digitone II slot over Web MIDI, keeps them in a local library and sends them back to a chosen slot; also imports project capture .syx files and replays a captured project stream. Proprietary. Shows that DN2 pattern/kit dump requests per slot work over SysEx (claim, not checked by us).

projects.name: MachineDrandom
projects.author: Kerem Ergener (per altstrument)
projects.notes: Closed-source browser app that randomises the loaded Machinedrum kit live over Web MIDI, engine by engine and parameter by parameter, and can generate rhythm patterns played as MIDI notes. Nothing is stored until the kit is saved on the unit. Proprietary.

projects.name: Say A! (MCL chromatic A tool)
projects.author: BartBral
projects.notes: Browser sample prep and transfer tool for the Machinedrum UW: shifts each sample so its root lands on an A for MegaCommand's chromatic mode, resamples, processes loops, and sends over MIDI Sample Dump or saves WAV and .syx. Licence not stated. Repo clone timed out (large); details from altstrument.

projects.name: SM (Machinedrum sample manager)
projects.author: Fyris
projects.notes: Closed-source browser sample manager for the Machinedrum UW using MIDI Sample Dump Standard over Web MIDI: 48 slots with waveform view, WAV and .syx import/export, reverse, invert, loop and name controls. Proprietary.

projects.name: Model:Cycles Web Editor
projects.author: tkawamu0622-cmd
projects.notes: Browser piano-roll editor and sequencer for the Model:Cycles over Web MIDI: parameters as CC, pattern select by program change, and recording a sequence into the unit one track at a time by playing it in over MIDI clock (no pattern SysEx). Licence not stated. Repo clone failed (transfer error); details from altstrument.

projects.name: BIAS (six-oscillator percussion machine)
projects.author: 100demons
projects.notes: Source package for a percussion machine with six oscillators, each with its own envelope, summed, wavefolded and given a second envelope, on a clock locked to the note; written clean-room after Noise Engineering's published description of the Basimilus Iteritas Alia (no NE code or tables per its notices). Fixed-point C for the ColdFire, a table generator, a host build and an emulator test on the OS's own voice loop. A machine package for model27, with a fixed-slot tweak for Modded Cycles 2.0; also on the Cycles Engines flasher. Played on a Model:Cycles 2026-11-03 in slot 11 (README): heavy on the processor, and it does not combine with five model27 Track FX packages (15 overlap problems). Commits a compiled object (bias.o). Found via altstrument 2026-11-04.

projects.name: CTRL+ / USER CFG (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: DigiAlchemydsp
projects.tested_note: shop: tested on hardware, stable
projects.notes: Adds the Digitone Keys' User Mode page (stock page 24) to the regular Digitone's TRIG page rotation, plus a USER CFG page that assigns the eight encoders; the assignment is saved with the project through core-dn1 project data. Testing status not stated. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-05.

projects.name: CHOKE GROUPS (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 3.1 or later
projects.notes: Two choke groups set per track from the Mod Menu and saved with the project: a note on a track fades out the voices of the group's other tracks over one 32-sample block (0.7 ms). Names no firmware address (uses ev_voice_on, ev_render_voices, fw_voice_track). Checked only in digiemu (11 voices choked, output RMS measured); not heard, not on a unit.

projects.name: PROGRAM CHANGE -> SOUND (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)
projects.notes: A program change on a track's channel loads that number's sound from the project's pool onto the track, as the SOUND BROWSER's FUNC + YES does (program 1 = pool sound 001). Checked only in digiemu, not on a unit.

projects.name: MIDI LOOPBACK (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)
projects.notes: An internal MIDI cable: what the MIDI tracks send on one chosen channel goes back into the unit as if from DIN, so a MIDI track sequences and p-locks a synth track or (on the FX channel) the master effects. Names no firmware address. Checked only in digiemu with its DIN output captured; the CC path only through core_midi_receive.

projects.name: SOLO & MUTE GROUPS (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)
projects.notes: Track key + FUNC solos a track among its four; four mute groups. Checked only in digiemu (with LOOPBACK and PC SOUND in the same build), not on a unit.

projects.name: ARP MENU (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)
projects.notes: A long FUNC + KEYBOARD opens the ARP menu (stock: FUNC + SYN1 at the other end of the panel); a quick press still toggles the arp. Checked only in digiemu; not on a Digitone Keys or a unit.

projects.name: Mezclando (transition mode for Digitakt II)
projects.author: Lucioic (Oicul)
projects.notes: A DJ-style mix mode on the SONG key: pick a reference pattern and bring its tracks, with their sequences and sounds, into the playing pattern one by one, with per-track levels, mutes and a one-step undo; YES loads the whole reference pattern with its kit (stock copy + paste). Uses only the firmware's own functions and stores nothing of its own; stock SONG functions move to FUNC + SONG and TRK + SONG. Built locally in a browser patch page or from source (m68k-elf GCC, Node 24, a Modwerk checkout with core-dt2 1.0). English and Spanish README. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-05.

projects.name: digimod (Digitakt II mod builder)
projects.author: endlea
projects.own_mods: [{"name": "Polyphony", "version": "0.2.0", "path": "mods/polyphony", "tested": "partly", "note": "v0.1 and the 0.2.0 voice fixes on hardware; the chord editor emulator only", "what": "VOICES 1-8 per track, borrowing the DSP channels of idle tracks; chords recorded per trig, a chord editor on the TRIG page"}, {"name": "Plaits", "author": "Em D (digikit); Plaits by Emilie Gillet; port to 1.16 by endlea", "version": "0.2", "path": "mods/plaits", "tested": "emulator", "note": "not on hardware", "origin": "digikit", "what": "Mutable Instruments Plaits as a PLAITS machine on the DSP: 25 models, four DX7 banks (port of digikit's Plaits as pinned by the Digitakt II All-in-One)"}, {"name": "Musical WAVE / Deja Vu", "author": "K\u00e1ri Gar\u00f0arsson; port to 1.16 by endlea", "version": "0.1", "path": "mods/musical-wave", "tested": "emulator", "note": "not on hardware in this form; Deja Vu V5.1 alone is hardware-tested on 1.16", "origin": "digitakt-ii-research", "what": "LFO WAVE values 7-15: Deja Vu random loops (fixed or new per trig) and seven scale quantizers for SAMPLE TUNE (K\u00e1ri Gar\u00f0arsson's D\u00e9j\u00e0 Vu V5.1 and Musical WAVE V4 from the Digitakt II All-in-One, ported from 1.17 to 1.16)"}, {"name": "One-Shot Zoom", "author": "K\u00e1ri Gar\u00f0arsson; port to 1.16 by endlea", "version": "0.1", "path": "mods/oneshot-zoom", "tested": "emulator", "note": "not on hardware in this form; V11 on 1.17 has hardware reports", "origin": "digitakt-ii-research", "what": "Zoom (1x, 2x, 3.75x) and pan the waveform on the ONESHOT SRC page with encoder C; display only (K\u00e1ri Gar\u00f0arsson's ONESHOT Zoom V11, ported from 1.17 to 1.16)"}, {"name": "System Load", "version": "0.3", "path": "mods/sysload", "tested": "partly", "note": "v0.1 page and DSP load on hardware; the v0.3 voice count emulator only", "what": "SETTINGS > SYSTEM > SYSTEM LOAD: DSP load (now, average, peak) and the voices in use"}]
projects.license: MIT (own code); mods derived from digikit and the All-in-One AGPL-3.0-or-later
projects.tested_note: per mod: each mod README says what ran on hardware
projects.contains: musical-wave (Deja Vu), oneshot-zoom, plaits, polyphony, sysload
projects.notes: A local web service (Docker, or native on macOS) that packs a Digitakt II .syx from ticked mods, checks it before download and, on a Mac, boots it in a built-in DT2 emulator. Mods: Polyphony (VOICES 1-8 per track, borrowing idle tracks' channels), Plaits (25 models and four DX7 banks on the DSP), Musical WAVE / Deja Vu, One-Shot Zoom and System Load; each mod's README says what was checked in the emulator and what on hardware. Notes that on hardware the DSP takes 7-12x longer than the emulator for one case. Also listed by altstrument. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-06.

projects.name: Digitakt LED colours
projects.author: ceredmeat
projects.notes: LED theme editor and standby light show: six themes plus CUSTOM, eleven colour families with RGB 0-31, trig-key previews, COMET / RAINBOW / BREATHE idle animations, settings restored at start-up. Tested only in digiemu (README: not on a physical Digitakt). Found by GitHub search 2026-11-06.

projects.name: MIDI Expression for the Digitakt (Digi-Expression)
projects.author: tekomelu
projects.notes: Pitch bend, mod wheel, aftertouch and breath controller from an external keyboard: modulation of audio tracks 1-8, pass-through to MIDI out on tracks A-H, velocity sensitivity per track, presets, saved with the project. A Modwerk SDK module, not submitted to the Modwerk library yet. Tested with host unit checks and in digiemu; ships a hardware stress-test script. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-05.

projects.name: Modded Cycles Techno Edition
projects.author: mbreilly (m_reilly)
projects.notes: 25 machines (Elektron's six plus 19: 909/808/606 voices, rumble kick, modal metal, additive drum, acid and growl basses, Braids, VA, cross-mod, 6-op FM, pad, and a sampler / granular / wavetable engine), a filter and insert effect per track, sidechain, master DJ EQ, 6-channel USB audio, CPU monitor and budget; plus a VST3/AU/standalone plug-in that follows the Cycles and reads sounds back. Built locally from the official OS (Python only), checked byte for byte. README: every part tested in emulation, and played on real hardware. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-05.

projects.name: Whiplash (agent plays a Digitakt II)
projects.author: hejijunhao
projects.notes: A Hermes Agent plugin that jams on a Digitakt II over USB MIDI: starts patterns by genre or mood, changes sounds live by CC/NRPN, mutes tracks (optionally the unit's own mute, CC 94); nothing is saved to the unit. Falls back to a virtual MIDI port without hardware. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-06.

projects.name: DBX-K2 (resonator kick for MDX)
projects.author: MonCalamari
projects.version: kick2-v0.9 (2026-11-06): HOLD replaces colour, pitch 38-160 Hz, saturation always on; v0.7 first release the same day
projects.notes: A DSP56300 user machine sent as SysEx into a USR slot: each trigger strikes a tuned resonator whose pitch falls from a higher start; knobs for base pitch, sweep depth and time, decay, attack pulse, hold, saturation and a low-pass tone. The release page lists cycle counts for the MKII and for the MKI with DRAM or SRAM and says it was tested on a MKII with the +Drive. Send the slot-1 .syx with about 300 ms between messages; it replaces USR slot 01. The author credits Claude with the DSP code and tooling. Per altstrument 2026-11-06 (the repo was empty on 2026-11-05).

projects.name: MUTINY (modular sequencers for Digitone mk1)
projects.author: mbaumannn
projects.tested_note: about an hour on one Digitone mk1
projects.notes: Three generative sequencers on the synth tracks: a Euclidean rhythm, a Turing Machine and a TB-303-style acid line, played from the encoders; YES writes what you hear into the pattern as ordinary trigs. The author tested it for about an hour on one Digitone mk1 (OS 1.44). Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

projects.name: DBX-DR (dark drone for MDX)
projects.author: MonCalamari
projects.tested_note: played on a MKII; MKI not played
projects.notes: Single-voice drone USR machine: three detuned saws and a square sub into saturation and a 4-pole ladder lowpass, with a phase-inverted feedback loop (gain up to 1.5, self-oscillating above 1) and WARP drift. Certified cycle counts per track and block: MKII 2,610, MKI DRAM 3,017, MKI SRAM 2,681; tested on one MKII +Drive UW, MKI certified but not played. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

projects.name: Elektron Project Companion
projects.author: Claptom-music
projects.notes: Windows editor for arranging live sets from local project backups: place patterns in banks A-H and export a new project for Transfer. Rytm MKII: .arprj and whole-project .syx (patterns, kits, sound locks, sample references). Digitakt II: .dt2prj project image v4 (patterns with their kits; merging only with identical sample pools, since relocating a sample changes locks). File-level testing on a real OS. Licence not stated. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

projects.name: sample-shepherd
projects.author: julesyoungberg
projects.notes: Organises a sample library (through Fourier Samples), exports it per device profile and syncs it to a sampler without breaking the projects on it: backs up projects, works out which samples they use, plans uploads and deletions and carries them out resumably; never deletes a sample a project uses. Elektron devices through elektroid-cli; used only with a Digitakt II so far (about 30,000 samples over a USB link measured at about 77 KB/s). Licence not stated. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07. 2026-11-10: the CLI reports sync progress as JSON events and stops a sync cleanly between files, for a planned desktop app.

projects.name: Model:Samples battery base
projects.author: malthelm
projects.tested_note: no physical prototype validated yet
projects.notes: Open-hardware battery base using the original side mounting points and the left battery input: editable CAD, STEP/STL, parts list, build guide and printable fit gauges. No working physical prototype validated yet. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

projects.name: SEND FX (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.notes: More from the Digitone mk1's own send effects and master drive: LUSH, a new bucket-brigade-style chorus in place of the stock one (VIBE, DRIFT, TONE, SAT, FDBK), two LFOs that move any chorus, delay, reverb or drive parameter (free or synced), and SHORT delay times. Written without Elektron code or tables. Checked in digikit's emulator. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

projects.name: Flex+ (FlexBus machine)
projects.author: DigiAlchemydsp
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.44 (core-dn1 4.0 + machines 0.2); Digitakt mk1 OS 1.54 (core 4.0 + machine-pages 1.1)
projects.version: 1.1 (2026-11-10; elemod files keep the machine revision 1.0)
projects.tested_note: 1.0: shop says both builds ran on hardware (the README had the Digitone build only); 1.1 linted and bench-tested, the new scope revision not yet on hardware
projects.notes: Routes the audio inputs or internal tracks into a track, with a low-CPU pitch shifter and an oscilloscope on the machine page. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07. 1.1: internal tracks are now tapped after the source track's filter and AMP (a track picking itself is silent), taller scope bars mirrored around zero that keep scrolling when audio stops, lower DSP and UI cost (about 4,246 instructions per block for one shifted bus), and an optional Digitakt build for FAST AUDIO that needs digihealth 1.0 (install it or the regular build, not both). Four playable parameters: TUNE, GAIN, MIX, INPUT.

projects.name: DigiArp MIDI (DA27)
projects.author: aleks-karachevtsev
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 OS 1.44; elekloader core 4.1.1 + seq-events 0.1
projects.tested_note: the exact DA27 module was installed and tested on hardware by the author
projects.notes: MIDI arpeggiator for the Digitone mk1's MIDI tracks A-D, each with its own settings, controlled from the stock ARP page and step editor: tempo sync, recorded MIDI trigs, the stock modes plus UP TWICE, DOWN TWICE and UP/DOWN REPEAT. Known issues and test results are documented. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

projects.name: STEP VIEW (Octatrack MIDI step editor)
projects.author: Slingdinger
projects.tested_note: built and tested in octabam's emulator; parts have run on the author's MKI
projects.notes: A step editor and piano-roll pitch view for the eight MIDI tracks (MIXER + MIDI): all tracks at 32 steps a row, one track's 64 steps, notes with VEL and LEN per step. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-08. 2026-11-11: the Split view also shows the audio tracks (each step's trig and its p-locks), and Pages with the audio tracks shows the cursor track's page values beside that page's SETUP.

projects.name: FERAL (nine noisy models)
projects.author: 100demons
projects.tested_note: played on a real Model:Cycles 2026-10-22 (standalone); the composed package build is new
projects.notes: One added machine with nine noisy, unpredictable synthesis models, light on the processor; COLOR and SWEEP as macros. Source package for the Cycles Engines flasher. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

projects.name: BLAST (OPL2-style FM)
projects.author: 100demons
projects.tested_note: README: emulator proofs passed; tested on a real Model:Cycles: not yet (read 2026-11-11)
projects.notes: One added machine with fourteen melodic two-operator FM models in the manner of the Yamaha OPL2 ('90s SoundBlaster). Source package for the Cycles Engines flasher. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

projects.name: PUNCH (OPL2-style FM percussion)
projects.author: 100demons
projects.tested_note: README: a voice-loop test in the source tree; tested on a real Model:Cycles: not yet (read 2026-11-11)
projects.notes: One added machine with twelve two-operator FM percussion engines with extended ratios. Source package for the Cycles Engines flasher. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

projects.name: ESOTERIKA (four Digitone voices)
projects.author: DigiAlchemydsp
projects.tested_note: shop: tested on hardware, stable
projects.notes: Four extra Digitone mk1 voices - RUIN, XTAL, VOID and CREPUS - as separate elekloader mods plus a combined ESOTERIKA file. Found in the elekloader mod shop catalogue 2026-11-08.

projects.name: Filter-FX (seven filter effects)
projects.author: DigiAlchemydsp
projects.tested_note: shop: both builds tested on hardware, stable
projects.notes: Seven filter-based effect modes per track: VOWEL, BANK, FOLD, CRUSH, RING, PHASER and FLANGER. Found in the elekloader mod shop catalogue 2026-11-08.

projects.name: octabam2elemod (octabam modules as elekloader mods)
projects.author: irpina
projects.tested_note: each build boots on an Octatrack MKII (2026-10-03); most features not yet tested on a unit
projects.contains: 33 files (shop, 2026-11-08): tuner, quantizer, repitch, direct-jump, rlen-plen, midi-scenes, scenes-p2, cc-map, cc-feedback, recorder-hold, recorder-spacing, flex-seekbind, lofi-amf-fix, USB MIDI, USB audio out (main, cue, master, tracks) and USB in/out crossbar variants
projects.notes: octabam's Octatrack modules repackaged as elekloader mods, so they can be picked in the elekloader mod shop. Found in the elekloader mod shop catalogue 2026-11-08.

projects.name: EUC+ (melodies for the Euclidean sequencer)
projects.author: joesciii
projects.tested_note: README: emulator only; the first hardware build (E201) not yet confirmed on a unit
projects.notes: Adds Torso T-1-style generated melodies to the stock Euclidean sequencer: each Euclid hit gets a note from a pool of scale degrees in the pattern's KB SCALE and ROOT NOTE, moved by a phrase shape and a seeded, lockable random sequence. Own NOTES and RANDOM pages opened from the stock Euclid page; off by default per track; works on audio tracks (repitched) and MIDI tracks; patterns stay stock; settings are lost at power-off for now. Hooks the end of the audio and MIDI step fire (0x400d6e10, 0x400d7234 on OS 1.17). Built from your own OS file with shell scripts for Linux; a research log and a design document come with it. Credits Aggregat's rules and device facts for its build checks and flash procedure. Found via the owner 2026-11-08.

projects.name: Digisophie-DN (SOPHIE for the Digitone)
projects.author: x2k77m1 (port); soejrd (Digisophie)
projects.tested_note: README: performance guidance is hardware-tested (one SOPHIE track safe), hardware photos of both pages
projects.notes: soejrd's Digisophie ported from the Digitakt mk1 to the Digitone mk1 / Keys: SOPHIE metallic percussion as machine 11 (SOPH) with four models - FUSE, BOOM, PIPE, SHARD - through the Digitone's own filter, mixer, effects and AMP envelope; knobs borrow stock SYN ranges. Shares the fixed-point DSP core with the Digitakt mod; one build per OS version. GitHub marks it a fork of digisophie; it adds its own Digitone machine adapter.

projects.name: ModelDigi (Model D oscillators)
projects.author: simonjohansson
projects.tested_note: README describes behaviour on the Digitakt and measurements against an original Model D; no explicit statement of a unit run
projects.notes: A Minimoog Model D-style oscillator section for the Digitakt mk1: three oscillators with their ranges, waveforms, tuning and levels, oscillator 3 as a pitch modulator of the others, slight pitch drift and mixer saturation (a switch per sound turns them off). Waveforms and modulation follow measurements of an original Model D. No filter, envelopes or amplifier of the Model D (the Digitakt's own are used). CPU-heavy: needs SETTINGS > FAST AUDIO on. Digitone support planned.

projects.name: Sidecar | Expander: Rytm mods
projects.author: trigcondition
projects.base_os: Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74 and 1.73; Analog Four MKII (a4/)
projects.notes: The source of the Analog Rytm MKII OS mods that Sidecar | Expander needs: patch sources, symbol map, allocation registry and the build that turns the user's own stock .syx into a modded one, as one elekloader module per OS; the Analog Four MKII's mod in a4/. 0.4.0 reports each track's pan and route (stereo through mode), adds MD's own page, preset browsers for JUNO and 6-OP FM, DSP SAMPLE's sample picker, list knobs of up to 36 names, a MIDI machine (machine 50) and arpeggiator settings in the sound. Sidecar Mini (Teensy) is frozen at 0.1.0.

projects.name: CyclesEmu (Model:Cycles engine as plug-ins)
projects.author: Jackherz
projects.license: not stated (JUCE under AGPLv3; bundled effects MIT)
projects.notes: Unofficial macOS plug-ins (AU, VST3, standalone) that run the Model:Cycles' own sound engine: the parts of the firmware that render audio are translated ahead of time from ColdFire code to C, from the user's own firmware (nothing included or derived in the repo). CyclesEmu (eight tracks with machines, LFOs, filter, mixer, delay and reverb), CyclesVoice (one sound, up to eight voices) and CyclesFX (the delay and reverb). The translated render matches the digiemu emulator bit for bit on captured blocks; eight tracks take about 11 % of one M1 Pro core. A personal research project.

projects.name: Mono Chorus CLAP
projects.author: nerazin
projects.notes: A small stereo CLAP chorus plug-in (macOS) after the Monomachine's FX-CHORS: a floating-point reconstruction with eight automatable parameters (DEL, DEP, SPD, MIX, FB, WID, LP, INP), one C file, no firmware and no emulator.

projects.name: DN2 Tools (dn2mk2 browser tools)
projects.author: De-Pattern
projects.notes: Browser tools (Chrome or Edge, Web MIDI) for the dn2mk2 Digitone II mod: DN2 Sample Import sends WAV files and folders to the mod's sampler over USB (replace all, choose slots, or add), plus tools for its recorder and the Machinedrum PERC machine. Hosted on GitHub Pages; the firmware itself is in De-Pattern/dn2mk2-firmware.

projects.name: elkbench (hardware tests as an MCP server)
projects.author: Iced-Cream
projects.notes: One local MCP server per PC that gives AI agent sessions the same tools for testing Elektron units (Analog Rytm MKII, Analog Four MKII, Digitone; Digitakt untested on hardware) and their emulators: claim a unit, run a test plan, flash an OS, take screenshots, record and check USB audio, take or restore an Overbridge Total Recall image. It enforces one owner per unit, emulator first, and a hardware run only after the person says go. Python stdlib; Windows and Linux. 2026-11-10: a flash between two fixed OS files of a unit can reuse an emulator pass of the same flash, recorded with the hashes of the emulator, the flash tool and the card, while all of them stay the same.

projects.name: sidecar-emu (Sidecar emulator)
projects.author: Iced-Cream
projects.notes: QEMU cut down to the Raspberry Pi 4B and the devices Sidecar's engine needs: boots the Sidecar engine image, answers over Ethernet, puts an Analog Rytm MKII stand-in on its USB-A side and gives its USB-C gadget a raw MIDI TCP port, so an OS upgrade or an elkbench run can go through the emulated Pi into analog-emu. A local experiment, not meant for QEMU upstream.

projects.name: Octacloudz
projects.author: davidecaldarola1-ship-it
projects.notes: Repo no longer reachable on 2026-11-08 (check_updates). Repo description only: a granular FX2 module for the Octatrack MKII in the spirit of Mutable Instruments Clouds. No README yet, so OS, loader, licence and tests are unknown. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-08.

projects.name: Analog Heat FX+ MultiMode (beta 0.1)
projects.author: sapfir365karat (elektronmods.com)
projects.notes: The first public custom firmware announcement for the Heat +FX (2026-11-02): screenshots only; features, OS version, licence and a unit test are not stated, a GitHub link is promised. Origin: elektronmods.com, read 2026-11-03. Re-read 2026-11-05: still no GitHub link, no description and no replies.

projects.name: selache (SHARC+ toolchain)
projects.author: js216 (ElekLabs keeps a fork)
projects.notes: Open-source toolchain for SHARC+ DSP (assembler/C compiler), GPL-3.0. Named in the dn2mk2 and dn2-cfw docs as the way to build Digitone II DSP code; ElekLabs/selache is a fork updated 2026-10-30. Original repo not read by us yet.

projects.name: dn-deobfuscator
