rules.title: Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section.
rules.text: A1. Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. Patch the main OS only. Then the stock OS file can always restore the unit. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} {elekloader-readme} {digikit} (ElekLabs README: patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8) {dn2mk2-safety} (dn2mk2 gate: sections 2, 4, 5 and 8 byte-identical to stock; mods change only 3 = MAIN OS and 7 = DSP) {digikit-old} (earlier README: 2 = bootstrap and 4 = updater never modified; sections 3 and 7 were the patch targets) {dn2-cfw} (brick checker refuses any bootstrap change).

rules.title: Know the recovery path before anything is flashed.
rules.text: A2. Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. Write it down in your output, with the exact button combination for the device (see [`common/recovery.md`](common/recovery.md)). Keep the stock OS file and, for Digitakt II / Digitone II, a physical DIN MIDI interface at hand. Note: digikit's README itself says recovery via the bootstrap menu is "not tested on hardware" - treat Digitakt II recovery as unproven, Digitone II recovery was exercised by dn2-cfw, Overtone and dn2mk2. `[doc]` {digikit} {digikit-old} {synthack-os} {dn2-cfw} Incidents: [I45](INCIDENTS.md#i45-recovery-used-on-a-digitone-mk1-after-a-logo-hang).

rules.title: Back up first.
rules.text: A3. Back up first. Back up projects/sounds (+Drive) with Elektron Transfer before flashing. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw} Incidents: [I47](INCIDENTS.md#i47-stock-storage-resets-did-not-create-the-sample-filesystem).

rules.title: Never power off during an upgrade.
rules.text: A4. Never power off during an upgrade. `[doc]` {elekloader-readme}

rules.title: BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step
rules.text: A5. BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step (DT2 startup menu; runs only if the incoming bootstrap version is strictly higher). Never build or send an image with a higher bootstrap version. Elektron's own notes add that some official upgrades also upgrade the bootstrap right after the first restart - never cut the power then. `[doc]` {digikit-old} {elektron-dt2-notes}

rules.title: Verify every candidate image before it is written
rules.text: A6. Verify every candidate image before it is written - re-read it, check all checksums, check that only the intended section differs from stock, check it fits the flash budget, check the main OS unpacks to exactly the patched image. elekloader does this per build; dn2-cfw additionally runs a 12-check brick checker. `[doc]` {elekloader-readme} {dn2-cfw} Incidents: [I40](INCIDENTS.md#i40-a-no-change-rebuild-came-out-2-bytes-short).

rules.title: First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down.
rules.text: A7. First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw} {dn2mk2-firmware-md}

rules.title: Gate what you ship.
rules.text: A8. Gate what you ship. Overtone and dn2mk2 only let the patcher save a file whose output hash matches a build that passed the project's own checks (Overtone: ~160 emulator checks per build; dn2mk2: `scripts/ship_gate.py` "CLEARED TO FLASH"). Do the same: no ungated output reaches a unit. `[doc]` {overtone} {dn2mk2}

rules.title: Respect transfer limits.
rules.text: A9. Respect transfer limits. Digitone II's USB upgrade receiver does not check the size limit of 2 MiB; oversized images stall at the end (nothing is written, a power cycle clears it). The withdrawn dn2mk2 builds v0.4-v0.7 hit this. Also keep the DSP image under 1,048,575 bytes. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-firmware-md} Incidents: [I3](INCIDENTS.md#i3-usb-upgrade-receiver-does-not-check-the-2-mib-limit).

rules.title: Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version.
rules.text: A10. Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. On Digitone II, Overtone needs stock OS 1.12 and dn2mk2 needs 1.11; getting from 1.12 to dn2mk2 means going back to a 1.11 base, and projects saved under the newer OS may not open. Always state the exact OS in the first line of a README. `[doc]` {overtone} {dn2mk2}

rules.title: Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash
rules.text: A11. Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash, and prove the transfer link with stock firmware first. Receivers have no error recovery (a dropped packet freezes the bar near 80 %), and recovery has so far been proven with stock images only. Full procedure in [`common/flash-procedure.md`](common/flash-procedure.md). `[hw]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety} Incidents: [I43](INCIDENTS.md#i43-recovery-stalled-at-80--the-midi-link-not-the-image), [I44](INCIDENTS.md#i44-recovery-used-on-a-digitakt-ii-after-a-crashing-build-a-cheap-cable-delivered-nothing), [I46](INCIDENTS.md#i46-syntakt-startup-menu-recovery-tested-over-din).

rules.title: One change per flash.
rules.text: A12. One change per flash. Never combine a new feature with a fix or a second patch in one image; keep the unmodified stock `.syx` untouched. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing}

rules.title: Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see.
rules.text: A13. Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. dn2mk2 runs `gate_hwrules.py` (complex-ping's `hwrules.py`) because DSP code that runs in the emulator can fail on silicon with DSP silence until power cycle. Use a comparable static check and keep to instruction encodings found in stock. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-safety}

rules.title: Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size.
rules.text: A14. Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. On the Digitone II the in-place loader of section 4 has a stock margin of +31,182 bytes and the default compressor setting turns that into -39,318, corrupting the image; the receive buffer is 2 MiB and the stock container is `0x1CC740` bytes. Use a packer that respects Elektron's stream limits (1 MiB window, 2,048-byte matches) and verify the margin of both stages. `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} {dn2-ele3} Incidents: [I39](INCIDENTS.md#i39-the-default-compression-level-corrupted-a-dn2-image).

rules.title: Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock
rules.text: A15. Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock, together with the bootstrap and updater. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} {dn2-ele3}

rules.title: Withdraw builds that lose sound.
rules.text: A16. Withdraw builds that lose sound. Digiwerk withdrew its six spring-reverb builds after finding that two of them stop the sound on a Digitone II; dn2mk2 withdrew v0.4-v0.7 for oversized images. Keep a visible list of withdrawn builds with the reason. When a build goes silent and the cause stays open, make the next test build audible about faults: Digiwerk sends the stock DSP's idle parks to a tone whose pitch names the fault ([I68](INCIDENTS.md#i68-spring-reverb-builds-lost-their-sound-on-a-digitone-ii-no-cause-found-offline)). `[hw]` {alt-digitone-ii} {dn2mk2-firmware-md} {dn2-cfw-mr03}

rules.title: In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit
rules.text: A17. In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit (Syntakt: empty reset and factory reset erase data); only TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE) belongs to recovery. State this in every recovery instruction you generate. `[doc]` {synthack-recovery}

rules.title: "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file.
rules.text: A18. "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. digitakt-ii-research's All-in-One v0.3.0 states in its install guide that "this exact release image is not hardware-tested", that a Plaits trigger click remains and that earlier Plaits builds failed normal Transfer updates at 0%/PREPARING. Put such statements next to the download and in the build log, not only in a changelog. `[doc]` {dt2-install}

rules.title: Red-team your own safety gate.
rules.text: A19. Red-team your own safety gate. Build deliberately unsafe candidates (patched upgrade validator, changed DSP, computed flash addresses) and make sure the gate refuses them; "incomplete" is never "accept"; protected ranges need exact end addresses. Details in [`common/agent-workflow.md`](common/agent-workflow.md). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-redteam}

rules.title: The progress bar is not proof.
rules.text: A20. The progress bar is not proof. On the Digitone II the recovery bar counts received packets only; the write and the decompression (next boot) come later, and a single bad packet stops the transfer silently. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap} Incidents: [I23](INCIDENTS.md#i23-plaits-builds-failed-normal-transfer-updates-at-preparing), [I43](INCIDENTS.md#i43-recovery-stalled-at-80--the-midi-link-not-the-image).

rules.title: Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly.
rules.text: A21. Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. On the Digitone II the "upload complete" event can be lost on the first upload after boot (unit stuck on "Receiving"); send Start without auto-commit, all blocks, then End(1); keep USB silent ~90 s while flash is written; one upload, no blind retries - look at the screen first. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-scripts} Incidents: [I4](INCIDENTS.md#i4-auto-commit-upload-loses-its-complete-event-on-the-first-upload-after-boot).

rules.title: Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path
rules.text: A22. Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path (Syntakt section 1 and bootstrap); a wrong configuration can harm analog circuitry. Do not emulate or reconfigure the FPGA; stub its status only. `[doc]` {digikit-f70}

rules.title: "Success! Rebooting" is not proof.
rules.text: A23. "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. The DT2/DN2 in-OS flash writer ignores erase/program return codes. Verify after reboot. Prefer the RPC route with an explicit End; send End 0 on every abort. Details: [`common/os-update-protocol.md`](common/os-update-protocol.md). `[doc]` {digikit-f75}

rules.title: Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`;
rules.text: A24. Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; never write the factory sample area (DT2 `0x458000-0x5D7FFF`). Lower areas can be overwritten by firmware, FORMAT or a crafted Data-API request. `[doc]` {digikit-f59}

rules.title: Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC).
rules.text: A25. Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). The stock engine fills a block to the edge without missing one. Code you add inside the Audio task must stop on a deadline measured from the block start, with margin, because one overrun drops a whole block. Put background work in a FreeRTOS task at priority 2-4, which cannot delay Audio. `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes}

rules.title: On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only.
rules.text: A26. On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. Words 1-6 and 677+ are rewritten by the firmware. Word k is at DM `base + 4k`, written to both copies. `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes}

rules.title: Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`.
rules.text: A27. Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. Everything above is cleared at boot. Never touch the bootstrap (it holds the STARTUP menu and recovery), the FPGA bitstream, or the MAIN OS factory console (`#UPGRADE`, `#FACTORY_DUMP`, calibration blob). `[hw]` {own-heatfx-notes}

rules.title: Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs.
rules.text: A28. Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. Use a write-back invalidation of the DM and PM caches together (`SHL1C_CFG`), then an instruction-cache invalidation, and keep the 12 instructions after every cache-register write 48-bit. Never mix invalidation and write-back-invalidation in one write. The emulator has no cache model. `[hw]` {digikit-f91} Incidents: [I15](INCIDENTS.md#i15-a-frequency-shifter-froze-the-unit-at-boot), [I35](INCIDENTS.md#i35-usb-replies-stayed-stale-for-minutes).

rules.title: Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops.
rules.text: A29. Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. Write a breadcrumb word (step, voice, type) straight into both reply records before each risky step, and keep a heartbeat. A stopped core never reaches the block-tail copy. On a stall, write a hang record to RAM that survives a soft reset (digikit uses `0x47fe0000`), then boot into a safe mode. digikit also enters safe mode when REC is held at power-on, and this worked on a Digitakt II; read the stock key state, since a scan of the input queue missed the key. Code that runs in the stock intro task is not covered by a handler installed later and halts the unit on a fault. `[hw]` {digikit-f48} {digikit-f77} {digikit-f117} Incidents: [I54](INCIDENTS.md#i54-safe-mode-by-rec-at-power-on-tested-on-a-digitakt-ii). On ColdFire boxes with storage, the firmware's own file primitives can write a text log to the card or drive (OctaMax did this on an Octatrack); this is often the only way to see code the emulator can't run. {octamax} octabam's soak script appends each reading as it reads it, so a total freeze still leaves its record ([I57](INCIDENTS.md#i57-a-demand-loader-soak-froze-an-octatrack-mkii)).

rules.title: Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock.
rules.text: A30. Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. The in-OS flash writer on DN2 1.12 has no length clamp and wraps addresses. A bumped section-2 version triggers the bootstrap self-upgrade on the next boot. Both are ways to lose recovery. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-t14} {dn2-cfw-t15} Incidents: [I3](INCIDENTS.md#i3-usb-upgrade-receiver-does-not-check-the-2-mib-limit).

rules.title: A negative is only as good as the search that produced it.
rules.text: A31. A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. Before you write "X is not there", run the same search on something you know is there. Say what the search covered (addresses, encodings, pages), and write "not found by <method>", not "not present". Every expensive wrong answer in dnfw's history was such a negative. Examples: - "no SHARC program in the update": it was a boot stream, not raw code; - "no upload path": it was on the DSPI next door; - "no references": the addresses live in another address space. `[doc]` {dn2-principles}

rules.title: Store each section the way the original stores it.
rules.text: A32. Store each section the way the original stores it. Some sections are aPLib streams and some are raw, and this differs between devices. Decide from the original (do its bytes depack?), never from an argument. A wrongly compressed or raw section passes every checksum and bricks the unit. Mirror the original's own integrity fields and re-verify the written file. `[doc]` {dn2-principles} Incidents: [I40](INCIDENTS.md#i40-a-no-change-rebuild-came-out-2-bytes-short).

rules.title: Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them.
rules.text: A33. Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. Both ran bit-exactly in the emulator and hung a real Digitakt II's DSP. Save I/M/L/B registers through an R register. Do SIMD compute on registers, and move data in SISD unless a one-variable probe image has proven the access mode on silicon. `[hw]` {dt2-plaits} Independently confirmed: digikit's unexplained "rung C" halt on a DT2 came from 17 such stores in a frame save. The SHARC manual excludes them (a store's source may not be a register of the DAG it addresses through), and the assembler and emulator accepted them. A build without them played on the unit. digikit's patchkit now refuses these encodings at build time. `[hw]` {digikit-f49} Incidents: [I14](INCIDENTS.md#i14-dag-registers-stored-through-their-own-dag-hung-the-dsp).

rules.title: On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget.
rules.text: A34. On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. The Syntakt's CPU #1 sits at ~89 % at rest, so a few thousand instructions per block make the UI lag. Measure cost per block in the emulator, keep a regression test, and make effects idle when silent. Never use RAM above the BSS for mod code on the Syntakt: sample loading overwrites it. `[hw]` {synthack-docs} {synthack-guide} On the Digitone mk1 an emulator cycle model even pointed the wrong way: it called a release faster while the unit's idle CPU rose from ~70 % to ~87 %. Only A/B builds on the unit decide. `[hw]` {tonefx-dev} Incidents: [I24](INCIDENTS.md#i24-a-granular-engine-froze-the-ui-at-low-pitch), [I49](INCIDENTS.md#i49-idle-paths-of-sixteen-mods-cost-two-percent-of-a-rytm-block). On the Octatrack, a 43 KB copy with interrupts masked held off the audio frame and clicked ([I60](INCIDENTS.md#i60-a-long-copy-with-interrupts-masked-clicked-on-every-reload)); on the Syntakt, code fetched from DDR cost far more than its instruction count and took MAIN to 100 % ([I64](INCIDENTS.md#i64-a-chorus-running-from-ddr-overloaded-the-syntakts-main-cpu)).

rules.title: Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts.
rules.text: A35. Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. Measured on a DT2 and a DN2: taken branches ~7 cycles, CALL+RTS ~14, a dependent float multiply chain 1.5 per instruction, hardware-loop start-up 12, and ~58 cycles for every L2 data miss. Buffers spaced at 16 KiB multiples fight over one cache set. Emulator counts underestimate all of these. `[hw]` {digikit-f103} Incidents: [I36](INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x).

rules.title: The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here.
rules.text: A36. The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. USB updates are received by the running OS. Before flashing anything that replaces or deeply changes the OS, make sure the user has a working DIN (or 3.5 mm TRS on Model:Cycles) MIDI interface and has sent a stock file through it once. A custom OS without the in-OS USB update leaves DIN as the only way back. `[hw]` {rytm-fw-re} {modded-cycles} {octabam} Incidents: [I22](INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path), [I23](INCIDENTS.md#i23-plaits-builds-failed-normal-transfer-updates-at-preparing), [I44](INCIDENTS.md#i44-recovery-used-on-a-digitakt-ii-after-a-crashing-build-a-cheap-cable-delivered-nothing), [I45](INCIDENTS.md#i45-recovery-used-on-a-digitone-mk1-after-a-logo-hang), [I46](INCIDENTS.md#i46-syntakt-startup-menu-recovery-tested-over-din).

rules.title: A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC).
rules.text: A37. A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). Stock's audio task waits inside its block, so "time outside the idle task" and stock's block-handler span both read ~80 % on an idle DN2 and *fall* to ~65 % with 64 notes held. To know whether added code fits, measure the deadline margin of the block itself (A25) under the heaviest stock load, not the busy percentage. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

rules.title: If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum).
rules.text: A38. If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). The OS re-flashes the boot code from its embedded copy when a version or magic check says so (A4 MK1: a newer embedded version; Machinedrum: magic `0x224B` missing at flash `0x3FFE`), so a stray byte there can become the recovery path. Locate the embedded image per OS version, keep every cave and pool outside it, and verify copy and check byte-identical to stock on the finished `.syx`. `[doc]` {a4mods} {rytm-mk1-mods} {mdkit-docs}

rules.title: Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver.
rules.text: A39. Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. On the Octatrack this froze a unit (a stale zero-length packet) and stalled OUT stages (stock leaves ZLT on). Size replies a byte short, or clear ZLT when you prime the stage. Send DMA'd replies from an uncached copy. Probably the same on every ColdFire box with the stock USB stack: the DT2 uses the same EHCI-style controller (queue heads in on-chip SRAM, EP0 max packet 64) and serves its own vendor requests on EP0 (digikit finding 42). Not yet measured there. On the DT2/DN2 the controller's transmit buffer is 64 bytes per endpoint: program every IN queue head you add for 64-byte packets, as stock does even where its descriptor says bulk 512; two 512-byte IN packets wedged a Digitone II's USB until a power cycle ([I70](INCIDENTS.md#i70-a-1024-byte-bulk-in-transfer-wedged-the-digitone-iis-usb-controller)). `[hw]` {octabam-traps} {modwerk-ot-traps} {digikit-f42} {digikit-usbfast} Incidents: [I5](INCIDENTS.md#i5-ep0-data-stages-of-a-multiple-of-64-bytes-stall-or-freeze-stock-usb-driver), [I6](INCIDENTS.md#i6-about-one-ep0-out-stage-in-50-100-goes-unanswered), [I70](INCIDENTS.md#i70-a-1024-byte-bulk-in-transfer-wedged-the-digitone-iis-usb-controller).

rules.title: Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator.
rules.text: A40. Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. An Octatrack change booted in the emulator and in quick power cycles, then stalled at the logo after minutes off. Emulators model neither reset settling nor RAM retention. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} Incidents: [I7](INCIDENTS.md#i7-a-soft-reset-leaves-the-usb-controller-running), [I34](INCIDENTS.md#i34-a-startup-change-stalled-at-the-logo-after-a-long-power-off).

rules.title: Disassemble what you assemble.
rules.text: A41. Disassemble what you assemble. Every community assembler for these chips has silently mis-encoded something: - octabam's `dsp_asm`: `tfr` as `rnd`, unknown `mpy` orders as `mpysu`, `cmp` as `max`; - selas: negative shift immediates; - the DSP56300 reference assembler: overlapping `ORG`s accepted silently. Incidents: [I15](INCIDENTS.md#i15-a-frequency-shifter-froze-the-unit-at-boot), [I27](INCIDENTS.md#i27-an-encoding-every-decoder-accepts-raised-ilopi-on-the-chip). Round-trip new code through a disassembler and compare, and make the build refuse a mismatch. `[hw]` {octabam-traps} {elekloader-adapting} {mdkit-docs}

rules.title: ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator.
rules.text: A42. ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. The forms below were excluded by ColdFire, ran in the emulator, and failed on a unit: Jump targets must be even: a jsr/jmp to an odd address raises an address error on the unit while the emulator runs on; elekloader's linker now refuses odd targets ([I61](INCIDENTS.md#i61-odd-jump-targets-froze-a-digitakt-ii-at-boot-the-emulator-kept-running)). Check that every routine lands in an executable section: code placed in `.bss` is zero-filled on the unit and stopped a Digitakt II with an illegal instruction, while the emulator ran the zeros as no-ops ([I67](INCIDENTS.md#i67-code-built-into-bss-crashed-a-digitakt-ii-at-boot-the-emulator-ran-the-zeros)). {digi2core} - `move.l #imm,d16(An)` (immediate to displacement) crashed a Digitakt II at startup with exception vector 4. digikit's machine builder wrote the same form (`2f7c imm 0008`, `move.l #imm,(8,A7)`) independently: it is 8 bytes long, and ColdFire instructions are at most 6 (the programmer's reference: "1 to 3 words", "limited to 3 sizes: 16, 32, or 48 bits" {nxp-cfprm}), so every image with that shim faults on a real ColdFire while the old generic m68k emulator ran it {digikit-f02}; - `move.l #imm,abs.L` (immediate to absolute) appeared five times in an early copier of a Digitone mk1 build, which then hung on the logo. It was the most likely cause, though the fault address was never captured. In the second case, a local ISA checker also accepted the form, because it decoded the instruction without checking the source/destination pair. Assemble with the right `-mcpu`, check hand-encoded bytes against the manual's mode tables (CFPRM pp. 4-47/4-48), and round-trip (A41). `[hw]` {dt2-lab-coldfire-fix} {dn1-arpmod-e04}

rules.title: A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit.
rules.text: A43. A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. Zero bytes in the image can be `.bss` that the engine writes only while it plays. A mod placed in such a region worked with the sequencer stopped and failed during playback (octatrack-mods, reported by rytm-mods-src). Before shipping into a new cave: fill it with a known pattern, flash, exercise playback, sampling, Overbridge and storage, and read it back. Combine this with static proof (no references) and emulator coverage (A4 MK1 practice), not instead of it. The same failure was seen on the Octatrack: tables lost to a heap tail (octamax), and a scratch word at `0x80006a60` overwritten under live recording on an MKI (KYOTI). This applies to data scratch as well as code. `[hw]` {rytm-mods-src} {a4mods} {kyoti-caves} Incidents: [I18](INCIDENTS.md#i18-the-flash-cave-reportedly-froze-a-unit-at-the-logo), [I19](INCIDENTS.md#i19-patching-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit), [I48](INCIDENTS.md#i48-a-menu-table-in-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit). Further cases: OCTAMAX state inside the stock audio-analysis buffer of the Octatrack silenced tracks ([I59](INCIDENTS.md#i59-patch-state-inside-a-stock-tasks-buffer-silenced-tracks)); a Synfact window in the zero tail of a Syntakt filter table was read as filter poles ([I63](INCIDENTS.md#i63-a-mods-memory-window-broke-the-basewdth-filter)).

rules.title: A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over.
rules.text: A44. A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. When a mod sheds voices to stay inside the audio budget: - Trigger on a peak that lasts several blocks or on a slow average. Isolated heavy blocks (a step with many trigs, caches flushed by the UI) are over before you see them, and cutting a voice then only adds an audible gap. - Keep fixed-point averages in scaled units. An integer `avg += (x - avg) >> 8` never moves, and the rule silently never fires. - Choose the victim by audibility after the mixer, and prefer muted tracks. On a Model:Cycles this turned "the last track always cuts out" into clean playback at 89 % peak. `[hw]` {supermodel-notes} A voice the governor drops must stay off until its next note: dn2mk2's guard retried a dropped sample voice every block, and an ONESHOT kick flickered and sounded crunchy beside heavy synth voices ([I71](INCIDENTS.md#i71-a-dsp-load-guard-dropped-a-sample-voice-block-after-block)). Render the cheap voices first, so time runs out on the expensive ones. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v048}

rules.title: Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2).
rules.text: A45. Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). The last 11 instructions of a hardware loop, and all of a loop shorter than that, must be legacy 48-bit instructions; the rest of the code may be compressed. Three projects reached this independently: - digikit: a selas defect left the end of a nested loop compressed, and `fx/freqshift` froze a real Digitakt II at boot while the emulator ran it ([digitakt-2.md](devices/digitakt-2.md)) {digikit-f91}; - the digitone-2-modding-skill checks it with `hwrules.py`, and stock DN2 1.11 obeys it in all 286 loops; its full list (loop end, `LCE`, CALL and branch spacing, same-DAG) is in [digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md](devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md) {dn2-skill-scripts}; - the DT2 Plaits port compresses everything else and keeps loop ends in ISA ([digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md](devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md)). Incidents: [I15](INCIDENTS.md#i15-a-frequency-shifter-froze-the-unit-at-boot). Wrap nested loops in `.NOCOMPRESS`, and check the rule on the disassembly (A41), since the emulator does not enforce it. `[hw]`

rules.title: Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2).
rules.text: A46. Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). The ColdFire depacks section 7 into a 1 MiB buffer and checks the size only afterwards, so a larger stream overruns the buffer before it is refused. One build with a 1,314,460-byte stream raised an exception on a unit. Run the stock depacker (or an exact copy) in the build and fail above the limit; zero regions can be fill blocks instead of stored bytes. Details: [firmware-container.md](common/firmware-container.md). `[hw]` {dt2-lab-capicola} {digikit-f06} Incidents: [I16](INCIDENTS.md#i16-a-decoded-section-7-over-1-mib-crashed-the-unit).

rules.title: Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2).
rules.text: A47. Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). The DN2's eMMC TRIM can report TRIM ERROR on a busy card: the stock busy wait arms its DAT0 interrupt before testing DAT0 and leaves a stale semaphore post, and the driver has no timeout. Read the eSDHC present state (`PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024`) before every TRIM and verify read and call only when DAT0 is high and no inhibit is set; retry an idempotent command a few times; let a long erase pause and resume instead of failing. Incidents: [I1](INCIDENTS.md#i1-stock-emmc-trim-fails-with-trim-error-on-a-busy-card). `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v040}

rules.title: Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized.
rules.text: A48. Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. On the DN2 the bootstrap leaves the data cache off, but the main OS turns it on for `0x40000000-0x47ffffff` only; the SSI DMA buffers stay uncached. Packing the SSI slots with byte-wise uncached reads stalled the sequencer; reading each of the 14 slots once as a 32-bit word did not. On the A4 MK1 only `0x40000000-0x43ffffff` is cached and ~1,000 uncached accesses per block per voice slowed the UI and could crash the unit. The reverse also bites: DMA reads RAM, not the copyback cache, so a reply the CPU wrote may go out stale. Copy hot state into cached memory (or the stack) once per block, work there, write it back; send DMA data through the uncached alias. Incidents: [I10](INCIDENTS.md#i10-byte-wise-reads-of-uncached-dma-buffers-stalled-the-sequencer), [I11](INCIDENTS.md#i11-uncached-state-in-a-chord-oscillator-slowed-the-ui-and-could-crash-the-unit), [I35](INCIDENTS.md#i35-usb-replies-stayed-stale-for-minutes). `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} {dn2-cfw-usb} {a4mods} {modwerk-ot-traps}

rules.title: Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit.
rules.text: A49. Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. A development unit carries state the users' units lack: armio's R012 mounted a sample filesystem it never created, and only new users' units (0 bytes in Transfer, stalled uploads) showed it. Before a release, flash stock, reset, then install the build as a new user would, and check every storage path it relies on. Incidents: [I12](INCIDENTS.md#i12-a-sample-machine-mod-could-not-create-the-storage-it-needed), [I47](INCIDENTS.md#i47-stock-storage-resets-did-not-create-the-sample-filesystem). `[hw]` {armio-samples}

rules.title: Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads.
rules.text: A50. Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. On the Octatrack, key events posted straight into stock's queues crashed the unit minutes later, and restoring DSP-read data every frame corrupted the audio. Feed the panel parser its own bytes; restore only CPU-side bookkeeping. (E2 is the same rule for stored sound data.) Incidents: [I30](INCIDENTS.md#i30-key-events-posted-into-stocks-queues-crashed-the-unit-minutes-later), [I31](INCIDENTS.md#i31-restoring-dsp-read-state-every-frame-corrupted-the-audio). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} {octamax}

rules.title: Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width.
rules.text: A51. Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. An Octatrack DSP frame engine stopped after 50.7 minutes because its counter saturated past `$7fffff`. Short tests do not reach such limits; let a build play for at least an hour with the busiest project you have. Incidents: [I32](INCIDENTS.md#i32-a-dsp-frame-counter-saturated-after-507-minutes). `[hw]` {octabam-traps} octabam's 118-switch demand-loader soak found a freeze no short test showed ([I57](INCIDENTS.md#i57-a-demand-loader-soak-froze-an-octatrack-mkii)).

rules.title: Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2).
rules.text: A52. Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). Per-sample stores to the Digitakt II's DDR output buffer crashed the unit while the emulator was bit-identical, and a per-voice DDR path can cost ~10x its instruction count on the DN2. Render into L2 and copy once per block; read int16 samples two at a time. Incidents: [I17](INCIDENTS.md#i17-per-sample-stores-to-the-ddr-output-buffer-crashed-the-unit), [I36](INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x). `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes} {dn2-skill-sharc}

rules.title: Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map.
rules.text: A53. Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. Emulators often map more than the hardware: Gearmulator maps the Machinedrum's flash at `0x0` and at `0x10000000`, but after the OS remaps CS0 nothing decodes the low window, so images with low-window pointers boot in the emulator and hang on the unit. Link through the address the running OS uses and scan images for the other one. Incidents: [I38](INCIDENTS.md#i38-low-window-flash-pointers-boot-in-the-emulator-and-hang-on-the-unit). `[hw]` {mdkit-docs} The DN2 emulator path reads low memory as zeros, which hid a wild read that froze units; dn2mk2 now traps every non-stock read below `0x40000000` in the emulator ([I65](INCIDENTS.md#i65-a-machine-kind-past-the-end-of-a-label-table-froze-digitone-ii-units)).

rules.title: Never include, commit or publish Elektron firmware
rules.text: B1. Never include, commit or publish Elektron firmware (original or modified), dumps or decompressed code. Ship patches that carry only the author's bytes plus hashes of the expected stock bytes. The user supplies the stock OS file. `[doc]` {elekloader-readme} {elektron-firmware-tool} {digitakt-ii-research} {dn2-cfw}

rules.title: Identify the stock file by hash (SHA-256) and refuse anything else
rules.text: B2. Identify the stock file by hash (SHA-256) and refuse anything else - modified files and other OS versions are rejected, not "adapted". `[doc]` {digitakt-ii-research} {synthack-os} {syntakt-workbench}

rules.title: Say what you are.
rules.text: B3. Say what you are. Mods are unofficial, unsupported, not affiliated with Elektron, and used at the user's own risk (may brick; Elektron's wording: modifications "may affect warranty coverage" and may prevent future updates - it does not explicitly say the warranty is void, so do not claim more than that). Put that in every README. `[doc]` all mod READMEs {elektronauts-policy}

rules.title: Respect the manufacturer's forum policy.
rules.text: B4. Respect the manufacturer's forum policy. Elektron's post of 2026-09-16 (updated 09-17) forbids, on Elektronauts and Elektron's official social platforms, sharing, requesting or linking to files, tools, repositories or instructions for modifying firmware, and developing or distributing firmware/hardware that makes unauthorized use of Elektron's IP; such posts are removed. General discussion stays allowed. It applies to legacy machines as well. Do not post mod links there. This aggregator lives on GitHub and links only to metadata. `[doc]` {elektronauts-policy}

rules.title: Never assume an old stock OS can be fetched later.
rules.text: B6. Never assume an old stock OS can be fetched later. Elektron no longer lists old firmware (downgrades can cause errors; older versions only by email) and community archives are incomplete - ask the user to keep their own stock files for every OS they flash, and record their SHA-256. `[doc]` {em-firmware-list}

rules.title: Respect each project's contribution policy - for AI agents too.
rules.text: B5. Respect each project's contribution policy - for AI agents too. elk-herd's README says issues, comments and pull requests generated by AI will be summarily rejected. Before opening an issue or PR in someone else's repo, read the README/CONTRIBUTING and disclose AI help where the project expects it. `[doc]` {elk-herd}

rules.title: Prove that what you ship contains none of the manufacturer's bytes.
rules.text: B7. Prove that what you ship contains none of the manufacturer's bytes. Overtone's patcher carries copy instructions over the user's own file plus its own bytes, and checks that no 16-byte run of its own bytes occurs in the stock OS. That turns B1 from a promise into a test. `[doc]` {overtone}

rules.title: One mod = one OS version.
rules.text: C1. One mod = one OS version. Addresses and stock bytes are version-specific (hash-pinned). A mod for Digitakt mk1 1.53 is refused on 1.54; Digitakt II 1.17 addresses do not carry to 1.18+. Porting = find every address again. Keep a separate build per OS version. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} {digitakt2-perform}

rules.title: Test ladder, in order:
rules.text: C2. Test ladder, in order: build -> lint -> emulator cold boot compared against stock -> a unit you can recover. A verifying build is well-formed, not proven to work. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.title: Record the test state of every build
rules.text: C3. Record the test state of every build as `hw` / `emu` / `untested` in the project metadata. Several projects ship builds that are lint-clean but "not yet run on a unit". `[doc]` {digislicer} {digichroma} {digitakt2-perform}

rules.title: Emulators do not prove real-time DSP behaviour.
rules.text: C4. Emulators do not prove real-time DSP behaviour. The earlier digikit README said "no audio"; the current ElekLabs Features that cross the ColdFire-SHARC boundary need both processors emulated together, or a unit: dn2mk2's BOUNCE passed a ColdFire-only gate and failed on units. On the Octatrack the DSP AMP envelope restart only showed as clicks on a unit. Incidents: [I58](INCIDENTS.md#i58-a-wavetable-machine-clicked-on-every-note), [I66](INCIDENTS.md#i66-a-feature-that-crosses-coldfire-and-dsp-passed-the-gate-and-failed-on-units). README has ColdFire + SHARC+ running together with audio, but the DSP "does not run in real time yet", and dn2mk2 reports the emulators do not model the two chips' timing. DSP overruns show up only on a unit. `[doc]` {digikit-old} Incidents: [I36](INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x).

rules.title: Windows:
rules.text: C5. Windows: the DN2 tooling needs an m68k objdump; use WSL. `[doc]` {dn2-firmware-explore}

rules.title: Report honestly.
rules.text: C6. Report honestly. "Nothing counts as working until it has run on my unit" is the standard the more careful authors apply. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw}

rules.title: Porting to a new OS version = re-locating, not re-applying.
rules.text: C7. Porting to a new OS version = re-locating, not re-applying. Diff decoded content, check bootstrap and updater separately, re-find every patch by masked pattern (`find`/`expect`) and pin the build by hash; inspect unfamiliar sections first. (Digitone II 1.11 vs 1.12 MAIN images share only their first 28 bytes.) `[doc]` {dn2-os-versions} {dn2-cfw-release-history}

rules.title: Give every check a control that fails when the checker is broken.
rules.text: C8. Give every check a control that fails when the checker is broken. dnfw's LFO4 bridge passed every check and then faulted on a Digitone II. Three checks had reported success about work they never did: snapshot harnesses cleared code that no real boot had run; a boot gate printed "Safe to flash" after an unrelated edit had deleted its coverage section; and an emulator call returned 0 for a value that was present. Use a key nothing set that must read back absent, a routine list that must not be empty, a coverage line that must appear. A green result from an untested instrument is not evidence. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4} Incidents: [I42](INCIDENTS.md#i42-checks-reported-success-about-work-they-never-did). Test a safety mechanism's first step end to end through the production code: Synfact's safe-boot trial passed unit tests that replaced the eMMC write with a double, then crashed every boot on a Syntakt because the real table had no write function. Incidents: [I62](INCIDENTS.md#i62-a-safe-boot-trial-crashed-every-boot), [I56](INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit). For UI lifecycle tests, replay the actual edit and its notifications without manually repairing the next view. Armio's sampler tests explicitly reselected SYN before turning the sample knob; that hid a Machine-change path which left the old view attached. The corrected replay fails on R020 and passes the R021/R022 fix. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incident: [I51](INCIDENTS.md#i51-the-sample-popup-did-not-open-after-switching-machines).

rules.title: After every install, open a project saved before it, and install the next build over the normal route.
rules.text: C9. After every install, open a project saved before it, and install the next build over the normal route. Old data meets new code only on the unit: a DN2 project with a stored row count out of range crashed stock and modded builds, Octatrack projects stalled when an effect layout changed, dn2mk2's MD/MM tracks went silent after an install, armio's USB audio repeated after a project change, and Overtone 1.0 broke the next USB update. A release test opens an old project and a stock project, changes project once, and installs the following build with Transfer. Incidents: [I2](INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I13](INCIDENTS.md#i13-usb-audio-repeated-old-audio-after-a-project-change), [I21](INCIDENTS.md#i21-md-and-monomachine-tracks-went-silent-after-an-install), [I22](INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path), [I28](INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). `[hw]`

rules.title: Calibrate the emulator against stock and the unit before trusting its numbers.
rules.text: C10. Calibrate the emulator against stock and the unit before trusting its numbers. Call stock routines in the emulator and compare with what they must return (complex-ping's check found that its SHARC emulator shifted every fractional multiply); measure one timing per project on the unit and carry the ratio (2x on the DT2 for DDR-reading code, 7-12x in one digimod case, a hard stop that overshot 3x as far). An emulator that agrees with itself proves nothing about silicon. The display is part of this: digikit's emulator showed intro frames upright that the panel showed upside down. Check one asymmetric picture on the unit before trusting the emulator's orientation. Incidents: [I36](INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x), [I37](INCIDENTS.md#i37-a-sharc-emulator-shifted-every-fractional-multiply), [I53](INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel). `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes} {digimod} {dn2-skill-md} The same holds for event fields: Modwerk read a knob's own push-button byte as FUNC, and an emulator reference screen lacked markers the unit draws. Incidents: [I55](INCIDENTS.md#i55-a-knobs-own-push-button-byte-was-read-as-func), [I56](INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit).

rules.title: Every failure or test on a unit becomes an incident, and every incident that teaches something general becomes a rule.
rules.text: C11. Every failure or test on a unit becomes an incident, and every incident that teaches something general becomes a rule. Record it in [INCIDENTS.md](INCIDENTS.md) with the next free I-number: unit and OS, what was seen, the cause and how it was found (measured, read from code, emulator, unknown), the fix, the status and the evidence level. Then either add a rule here or add the incident to the rule it confirms, and mark the fact in the device page with `(I<n>)`. Rules grow from tests, not from opinion.

rules.title: Before you blame your mod, check [STOCK-BUGS.md](STOCK-BUGS.md) and reproduce the misbehaviour on the unmodified OS with the same steps; a stock bug you find goes into that list.
rules.text: C12. Before you blame your mod, check [STOCK-BUGS.md](STOCK-BUGS.md) and reproduce the misbehaviour on the unmodified OS with the same steps; a stock bug you find goes into that list. The reverse holds too: before you call it a stock fault, check that your own watchdog does not mistake one of stock's deliberate pauses for a fault - Modwerk's Octatrack base read the DSP pause of USB DISK MODE as a stall ([I69](INCIDENTS.md#i69-a-mod-took-stocks-usb-disk-mode-pause-for-a-dsp-stall-and-kept-the-audio-off)). Mods reach stock paths, and stock paths have bugs: a Part change by a mod shows the Octatrack's carry-over bug exactly as a stock pattern change does, and a damaged project halts stock and modded Digitone II builds alike. Record a new stock bug with the device and OS, the trigger, the cause if known and how it was found, and your workaround. Incidents: [I2](INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject} {kyoti-bugfixes}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Prefer events over raw patch sites.
rules.text: D1. Prefer events over raw patch sites. The core mod owns the shared hook sites; subscribe via its event bus, do not patch core-owned sites. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Patch whole instructions only.
rules.text: D2. Patch whole instructions only. A site that ends mid-instruction is refused. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: No overlapping claims.
rules.text: D3. No overlapping claims. No two mods may patch or claim overlapping bytes, memory or named resources. Declare resources (`sysex:`, `settings:`, `drive:`, `ui:`, `machine:` names; other memory as regions). `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Prefix every global symbol with the mod id, make internals `static`.
rules.text: D4. Prefix every global symbol with the mod id, make internals `static`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} Incidents: [I41](INCIDENTS.md#i41-a-label-defined-twice-resolved-to-the-wrong-file).

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Let the linker place code and data, never hard-code addresses.
rules.text: D5. Let the linker place code and data, never hard-code addresses. Sections allowed: `.run`, `.fast`, `.bss`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Custom machine IDs are permanent once kits store them.
rules.text: D6. Custom machine IDs are permanent once kits store them. Range 4-127. Claim `machine:<id>`. Known claims (Digitakt mk1, core 2.1): 4 = NEIGHBOR, 5 = DIGISLICER. Pick a free ID, then register it in [`devices/digitakt.md`](devices/digitakt.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} D6b. Digitone II machine IDs: synths 5-31 and filters 6-31 are separate namespaces, permanent, and there is no allocator - agree IDs with other authors before shipping; saved sounds of an absent mod keep their ID and show as MISSING. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2} D6c. Analog Rytm MKII mod machines take the hidden slots 34-43 (from elekloader core-ar2 0.13 also the TEST slots 44-52), claimed as `machine:<slot>`. Kits store the slot; on a build without the mod the kit loads it as DISABLE. elekloader refuses two mods with the same slot, and Modwerk also records claims on its agent board. Each slot has fixed knob positions, so give meaning to a sound index, not to a knob letter. `[doc]` {modwerk-rytm-machines}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Do not mix format 1 (whole build) with format 2 (linkable) mods
rules.text: D7. Do not mix format 1 (whole build) with format 2 (linkable) mods - whole builds cannot be combined. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Keep the audio interrupt handlers (`ev_render_in/out`) short.
rules.text: D8. Keep the audio interrupt handlers (`ev_render_in/out`) short. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Licence everything with an SPDX identifier and matching file headers.
rules.text: D9. Licence everything with an SPDX identifier and matching file headers. The ecosystem is mostly GPL-2.0-or-later (elekloader family); MIT and AGPL-3.0 also occur. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Disclose AI-generated code
rules.text: D10. Disclose AI-generated code the way DT-FM does ("largely AI-generated, not proofread"). Not a technical rule, but readers decide on risk from it. `[doc]` {dt-fm} D10b. Device-specific core rules (elekloader ADAPTING.md, 2026-10): Digitakt II has no render events (audio runs on the DSP) - subscribe only `.run` code to `ev_key`/`ev_enc` before the first tick; Digitone II has no `.fast` code (such mods are refused), remote panel input uses `core_keys_set`/`core_keys_clear`, SysEx uses `ev_sysex`, SHARC mods run at the master output in 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz with a 428-byte stack; RAM budgets: Digitakt mk1 128 KB (256 KB with core 4.0) plus 2,304 B fast SRAM, Analog Rytm MKII 128 KB and no fast SRAM; Digitone mk1 core 4.1.1 changed SETTINGS-row allocation (before it two rows could stall a first boot); each feature needs a minimum core version in `resources.core`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: An address that exists or maps onto another is not thereby free.
rules.text: D11. An address that exists or maps onto another is not thereby free. Prove an area unused (stock data pointers, caches, DMA buffers, boot ROM sharing) before placing code or data there; an unreferenced-looking L2 block once stopped a unit from starting. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {dn2-skill-firmware} Incidents: [I19](INCIDENTS.md#i19-patching-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit), [I20](INCIDENTS.md#i20-mod-code-at-a-free-address-crashed-projects-with-certain-samples), [I29](INCIDENTS.md#i29-dsp-scratch-at-84-and-up-hung-the-unit), [I33](INCIDENTS.md#i33-module-state-on-a-load-meter-counter-gave-a-jittery-pitch), [I48](INCIDENTS.md#i48-a-menu-table-in-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit).

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Budget voices, not tracks.
rules.text: D12. Budget voices, not tracks. Dynamic voice allocation can need far more voices than tracks; guard the DSP frame time and expose a CPU indicator. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports} Incidents: [I24](INCIDENTS.md#i24-a-granular-engine-froze-the-ui-at-low-pitch).

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Keep a trap register in your agent file.
rules.text: D13. Keep a trap register in your agent file. Known entries: OLED y runs bottom-to-top (`63 - y`; elekloader `ev_draw`: y=0 is the bottom row); on DT2/DN2 the stock intro's bitmap uses another layout than the main-UI blit (pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, measured on a DT2; [I53](INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel)) {digikit-f117}; compile ColdFire code with `-fno-ipa-sra` when using `-O2` (reported to corrupt interrupt pointers); `-mcpu=5475 -Os` is what the Digitone II skill uses; no libc (zero-initialised locals become `memset`). Add each new surprise when you meet it. `[?]` {dubspot} {dn2-skill-coldfire}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Fail closed.
rules.text: D14. Fail closed. If any anchor (stock hash, symbol, instruction pattern) does not match, build nothing or boot stock - never patch "close enough". `[?]` {dubspot} {elekloader-format}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: Disclose AI assistance
rules.text: D15. Disclose AI assistance where the community expects it (several projects require it; elk-herd rejects AI-generated issues/PRs). `[doc]` {dubspot} {elk-herd}

rules.section: D. Writing mods (format-2 / linkable, Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1)
rules.title: A hook on a hot path must cost nothing while its mod is idle: test first, then call.
rules.text: D16. A hook on a hot path must cost nothing while its mod is idle: test first, then call. dnfw's LFO4 hooked `memcpy`, `memset` and the per-frame LFO evaluators, and paid a call on every copy and frame even with no fourth LFO in use. Playing alone it was inaudible, but SAVE PROJECT while a pattern played stuttered until the save ended (whole-project serialise +6.3 %). The fix was an early exit in the stub (empty table or a block smaller than a sound: straight back) and skipping an idle LFO; stock then saved clean. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4}

rules.section: E. Changing parameter tables / saved data (Digitone II)
rules.title: Projects store values by slot, not by table row.
rules.text: E1. Projects store values by slot, not by table row. Details and the P-lock trap in [`devices/digitone-2.md`](devices/digitone-2.md). Moving the OS parameter table does not by itself change the saved format. New rows are only safe if they follow the author's growth rules (`docs/parameter-table-growth.md` in dn2-cfw - not yet read by us). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw}

rules.section: E. Changing parameter tables / saved data (Digitone II)
rules.title: Persist a mod's own sound parameters through the stock edit event, not a writer of your own.
rules.text: E2. Persist a mod's own sound parameters through the stock edit event, not a writer of your own. On the Digitone II (1.11) an edit is written into the stored sound record at once, so unsaved edits survive a power cycle; the writer is `Sound::updateMirror` (`0x4004ca80`). dnfw's LFO4 values did not survive until its setter sent the stock whole-sound event (`SoundConfigChangedInfo`) through the sound's holder; `updateMirror` then re-serialised the sound with LFO4's lane. Confirmed on the unit: unsaved LFO4 edits survive a power cycle, and SAVE PROJECT stores them. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4}

rules.section: E. Changing parameter tables / saved data (Digitone II)
rules.title: Keep every stored count and select value in range, and stamp old projects after a layout change.
rules.text: E3. Keep every stored count and select value in range, and stamp old projects after a layout change. Stock trusts what it loads: the DN2's song LOAD copies a stored row count without a check (21,503 rows instead of at most 99 crashed stock and modded builds alike), and an Octatrack select value outside its count stalled the sequencer on first play after an effect's layout changed. Clamp every count and enum a mod writes; when a build changes a stored layout, rewrite old projects' values on load. Incidents: [I2](INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I28](INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject}

rules.section: E. Changing parameter tables / saved data (Digitone II)
rules.title: Store a mod's data only where it differs from the defaults.
rules.text: E4. Store a mod's data only where it differs from the defaults. Every record a mod adds is written and checked on each save and load: Synfact's ARP mod sealed a carrier for every kit even with default settings, and a user saw project load and save slow down; leaving default carriers absent cut the serialization by 81 % in the emulator. Let "absent" mean "default", remove a record when it returns to default, and keep old projects readable. Incidents: [I50](INCIDENTS.md#i50-mod-data-written-for-default-settings-slowed-project-load-and-save). `[doc]` {synfact-lifecycle}

rules.section: E. Changing parameter tables / saved data (Digitone II)
rules.title: Test incremental working-state persistence separately from SAVE PROJECT.
rules.text: E5. Test incremental working-state persistence separately from SAVE PROJECT. A mod's companion can pass explicit save/reload while remaining stale in the unsaved working backup. On DN2 1.11, native settings updates bypass the whole-project serializer; armio's sample extension missed that path. Exercise load, change and unload through real notifications, serialize the working backup, then restore into a fresh emulator without retaining its heap. Keep current-project ownership/UID checks and the same lock as pool mutations; do not replace a saved checkpoint or add storage work to the shutdown interrupt. A passing replay does not prove physical power-loss recovery or that a frozen task completed its queue. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incident: [I52](INCIDENTS.md#i52-new-project-samples-were-missing-after-reboot).

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F1. Back up first, via Elektron Transfer and by re-reading the destination pattern; abort if the backup fails. `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F2. Allowlist the exact OS builds you have tested; refuse others. `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F3. Change only the bytes that must change, then read back and byte-compare. `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F4. Work on throwaway projects while a format is still being decoded; trust only mappings with a hardware-confirmed level (SYXGRID level A). `[doc]` {syxgrid}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F5. Never run parsers across device generations (Digitone mk1 device ID 0x0D vs Digitone II, Analog Four gen-1 vs gen-2). `[doc]` {syxgrid} {digi-roll-studio}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F6. Treat file-write / delete commands of the +Drive API as dangerous: only single-chunk writes were hardware-verified; move/copy/delete are not implemented anywhere we know. `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio}

rules.section: F. Writing to a unit over SysEx (control-side tools)
rules.text: F7. Close every other application on the port (Transfer, Overbridge, DNX) before a client run, and check every reply's length. With Overbridge holding the port replies were cut at exactly 885 bytes; with Transfer open a preset list showed 35 of 256. Incidents: [I9](INCIDENTS.md#i9-a-second-application-on-the-port-corrupts-sysex-replies). `[hw]` Full loop, spec questions and triage in [`common/agent-workflow.md`](common/agent-workflow.md). Short form:

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.text: G1. Ask the spec questions in one round before building. G2. Reproduce every bug as a failing test with a stock control before fixing it.

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.text: G3. Test what the hardware consumes, never by reading back what your own patch wrote. G4. Run emulator and static checks before every flash; the unit should only judge sound and feel. G5. Flash one clearly named image with its SHA-256 and a list of what to try; never overwrite older images.

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.text: G6. After two failed flashes on the same problem stop and restate goal, proven facts, unknowns and options. G7. Ask the user before cloning or installing anything.

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.text: G8. Keep levels honest: measure worst cases, add no unrequested gain compensation, clamp audio output, never read memory you did not write. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-md} {dn2-skill-workflow} Incidents (G8): [I8](INCIDENTS.md#i8-power-on-ddr-holds-garbage-often-a-nan), [I72](INCIDENTS.md#i72-a-drum-machine-mod-played-silent-hits-after-power-up-and-misread-stocks-voice-start) (a stock flag found set at power-up; a wrapper that passed two of three arguments).

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.title: Repo conventions to adopt from elekloader's AGENTS.md:
rules.text: G10. Repo conventions to adopt from elekloader's AGENTS.md: never weaken a check to make a test pass; a skipped test is not a pass - report which tests ran; keep device facts in profile files; check whether a core event already exists before adding a code site; keep byte-exact writer tests. `[doc]` {elekloader-agents}

rules.section: G. Working method (from the digitone-2-modding-skill - the one public agent skill that shipped a firmware mod)
rules.title: DSP rules the emulators cannot check
rules.text: G9. DSP rules the emulators cannot check (Digitone II, each reportedly silenced or crashed a real unit): whole 32-byte boot blocks, stock instruction encodings only (incl. sign bits of negative shift immediates), PRM loop/DAG/branch rules, no L2 above `0x200B0000`, never read unwritten DDR (power-on NaN), preserve registers at hooks (clobbered R8 at the FX-bus mixer hook lost all audio), count memory accesses not instructions. Details and addresses in [`devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md`](devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md). `[hw]` {dn2-skill-sharc} Incidents: [I8](INCIDENTS.md#i8-power-on-ddr-holds-garbage-often-a-nan), [I25](INCIDENTS.md#i25-clobbering-r8-at-the-fx-bus-mixer-hook-lost-all-audio), [I26](INCIDENTS.md#i26-a-boot-block-of-8n4-bytes-left-the-unit-silent), [I27](INCIDENTS.md#i27-an-encoding-every-decoder-accepts-raised-ilopi-on-the-chip).

conflicts.topic: DN2 SHARC L2 between `0x200918c0` and `0x200c2000`
conflicts.a: in use: stock data words point to `0x200918c0`, `0x200c0008` and `0x200c1f84` (dnfw), so Digiwerk keeps new data out of the whole range and lists `0x2008823c-0x200918c0` and `0x200c2000-0x200fa000` as candidates
conflicts.b: usable: the DN2 modding skill places boot blocks at `0x20090000` (code) and `0x20098000` (data), hardware-proven, and sets the ceiling at `0x200b0000`; elekloader's master-output mod (`0x20090000-0x20098000`) ran on a unit for ten minutes, and its machines take `0x20090000-0x200b0000`
conflicts.details: Both can hold if the pointed-to objects are small or unused in the cases tested. A pointer into the range is not proof of a write. Settle with a run-time write watch over `0x200918c0-0x200c2000` during playback, pattern changes and a save, or a canary read back on a unit. Until then: either stay below `0x200918c0`, or treat code there as tested only for the cases run. [`devices/digitone-2-internals.md`](devices/digitone-2-internals.md), [`devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md`](devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md) Unit evidence for the usable side, in part (dnfw, 2026-11-02/03): Waverider 0.3.9's level builder runs from L2 `0x200b0000-0x200b1900` (dn2_firmware_explore #335) and passed unit tests (builds wrl2a, wrl2b: tables sound as before, DSP load as before, a new table plays within about a second). It stays clear of the words at `0x200c0008` and `0x200c1f84`.

hypotheses.inference: Each unit has three different ids: SysEx device byte, product id, Overbridge USB id. Expected: DT2 `0x14` / `0x2A` / USB `0x0B2B`; DT1 `0x0A` / `0x0C` / `0x0B2C`; DN2 `0x15` / `0x2B` / `0x0B34`; Heat +FX `0x13` / `0x20` / `0x0B53`. The USB id's low byte changes with the USB mode (`0x012B` MIDI, `0x102B` audio/MIDI on the DT2).
hypotheses.test: Read the USB ids in each USB mode (`lsusb` on Linux, System Information on a Mac, Device Manager on Windows). Read the product id with Elektroid's device info.

hypotheses.inference: Unsaved edits survive a power cycle on the DT2 and the DT1 as on the DN2, because the stock edit writer stores each edit in the sound record at once.
hypotheses.test: On a throwaway project, turn a filter knob, do not save, power-cycle. Is the value still there? Also try a parameter lock.

hypotheses.inference: A received pattern dump lands in the slot armed on the unit, not in the slot its index byte names (shown on the DN2 by syxgrid).
hypotheses.test: On a throwaway project, send a pattern dump with index A05 while A02 is armed, using Elektroid or digi-roll. Where does it land?

hypotheses.inference: The DT1 recorder holds at most 33.0 s (1,584,000 frames at 48 kHz, mono).
hypotheses.test: Record with free length until it stops; time it.

hypotheses.inference: Overbridge rejects a modified OS whose container version field differs from stock (shown on the DN2, Digiwerk OB01).
hypotheses.test: No new flash needed if you already have builds: does Overbridge connect to a build whose version field was changed, and to one where it was kept?

hypotheses.inference: The Heat +FX answers the screen request (RPC framing `F0 00 20 3C 10 00`), as the Heat MKII does, so its screen can be mirrored and read without a mod.
hypotheses.test: Open Elek View (bluesgl.github.io/Elek_View) with nothing else on the MIDI port, select the unit, Start.

hypotheses.inference: The stock start-up animation runs at 30 frames per second, so it lasts about 5.8 s (175 frames), not about 11.7 s at 15 fps (O20).

hypotheses.test: Film a cold start with your phone, three times, and time the animation from its first frame to its last; also say whether it looked the same each time (one of five animations is picked at random, the first about 99.9 % of the time).

hypotheses.inference: The ~4 KB cut in long MidiRpc LIST replies is in the stock reply router, not in a mod: an unpaged listing of a 256-entry table store on a modded DN2 came back as 3,997 bytes, correct up to entry 125 and garbage after; pages of 64 were clean.
hypotheses.test: On stock, list a +Drive folder with more than 130 entries in one unpaged request (DNX or Elektroid) and compare the reply length and the tail with a paged listing. Until settled, page listings at 64 entries or fewer.

hypotheses.test: Back up first. On a throwaway project, put a small non-audio file on the +Drive with Elektroid, LOAD TO PROJECT, note what happens; then power-cycle, delete the file and run CREATE NEW before the next OS update.

hypotheses.test: With the USB probe: find the ready table and the running-task pointer, sample them 60 times.

hypotheses.test: A canary in the cave, read back after a cold boot and after playback. Combine with H9.

hypotheses.test: A canary or a write watch over the range during playback, pattern changes and a save (T24).
