hypotheses.test: A canary at `0x46700000`, read back after loading a large sample or project from +Drive.

hypotheses.inference: Direct hook writes may race reply publication on a DN2. Digikit measured 3,995 of 4,000 zero diagnostic words on a DT2; its own diagnostic clears overwrote the previous block's record in the DN2 emulator. Silicon DMA timing remains unmeasured.
hypotheses.test: Compare a hook's direct counter writes with static-word publication at block tail, without clearing prior reply records; count arrivals on the ColdFire side.

hypotheses.inference: SIMD loads or stores into L2 byte space hang the DN2's DSP as they hang the DT2's (same core, same IMASK).
hypotheses.test: A one-variable probe image with one SIMD L2 access behind a key press; recovery by power cycle.

hypotheses.inference: The SHARC's IIR0/FIR0 accelerators compute on the DT2 exactly as measured on the DN2 (output from stored word 5, FIR sums in pairs, INIDX/OUTIDX written the other way round).
hypotheses.test: Port the accelprobe image to the DT2 and compare the 76 result words.

hypotheses.inference: On the DN2, a single late DSP block is a one-block dropout that recovers, as on the DT2; the "silence until power cycle" reports came from sustained overload.
hypotheses.test: Provoke single late blocks (a burn loop on a key press) and count them on the DSP side; then hold an overload for seconds.

hypotheses.inference: Heat +FX builds need a cold-start test like other ColdFire units: a startup change can pass quick restarts and fail after minutes off (A40).
hypotheses.test: For the next startup-touching build: power off for 10 minutes before judging.

hypotheses.inference: Code costs on the Heat +FX follow the DT1's ColdFire lessons (EMAC mode switches, D16 hot-path hooks), since both run audio on an MCF5441x ColdFire.
hypotheses.test: Measure an audio-ISR hook with and without a MACSR switch per block.

hypotheses.inference: DT2 OS 1.17 saves only the kits the user changed, so a module's own kit data that changes by itself is lost unless a stock parameter of that kit changes too.
hypotheses.test: Modwerk publishes a unit procedure: change only module data, save, power-cycle, reload.

hypotheses.inference: The Octatrack stall after a PROJECT > SYSTEM walk on Modwerk builds is Modwerk's DSP stall watchdog firing while stock itself holds the frames (USB DISK MODE), not a stock fault.
hypotheses.test: Make the same walk on a unit with nothing installed, then with the watchdog off.

hypotheses.inference: The total freeze in octabam's demand-loader soak (I57) is the ColdFire spinning in one of the frame interrupt's waits that have no time limit, after the DSP stopped taking host words.
hypotheses.test: Add time limits (with a counter) to both waits and repeat the 118-switch soak.

incidents.title: Stock eMMC TRIM fails with TRIM ERROR on a busy card
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11 (dn2mk2 v0.39, erasing mod data), 2026-11-05
incidents.seen: TRIM ERROR at sector 817905, after a restart further on at CB1905.
incidents.cause: after CMD38 the stock busy wait arms the DAT0 edge interrupt before it tests DAT0; a short TRIM that finishes in between leaves a stale semaphore post, so the next TRIM on a really busy card returns at once and the call after it gets no answer. The driver has no timeout.
incidents.cause_found_by: read statically from stock code, not seen on the bus
incidents.fix: read `PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024` before every TRIM and verify read, call only when idle; retry five times; ERASE PAUSED and resume on request (v0.40).
incidents.status: fixed in the mod; the stock race remains.

incidents.title: Stock song LOAD trusts a stored row count
incidents.seen: one project crashed stock and modded builds alike when opened.
incidents.cause: song LOAD `0x400dea6a` copies `count` stored rows without checking it; the project held 21,503 rows instead of at most 99.
incidents.cause_found_by: read statically and confirmed on the project file
incidents.fix: repair the project (row count at record `+0x147`, storage version 4); mods must keep every count in range.

incidents.title: USB upgrade receiver does not check the 2 MiB limit
incidents.seen: an oversized image stalls at the end; nothing is written; a power cycle clears it.
incidents.cause: the receive buffer is 2 MiB and the receiver does not check the size.
incidents.cause_found_by: seen on the unit
incidents.fix: keep the container under `0x200000` bytes.

incidents.title: Auto-commit upload loses its "complete" event on the first upload after boot
incidents.seen: the unit sits on "OS UPGRADE / Receiving".
incidents.cause: with auto-commit the OS posts "upload complete" while the upgrade view is not open yet; the event is lost.
incidents.cause_found_by: read from stock code, seen on the unit
incidents.fix: upload without auto-commit, then send End(1), which checks the bytes and posts the event itself.

incidents.title: EP0 data stages of a multiple of 64 bytes stall or freeze (stock USB driver)
incidents.seen: the request after a 64/128/192/256-byte reply returned 0 bytes; once the unit froze. 128/192-byte OUT stages never completed.
incidents.cause: stock leaves zero-length termination on in the EP0 OUT queue head.
incidents.cause_found_by: measured on the unit
incidents.fix: size replies a byte short, or clear ZLT when priming.

incidents.title: About one EP0 OUT stage in 50-100 goes unanswered
incidents.seen: host requests time out now and then.
incidents.cause: the stage completes inside the ISR after stock's poll, or stops part-way.
incidents.cause_found_by: measured on the unit
incidents.fix: a 60 Hz tick finishes a completed stage, or stalls EP0 after 0.5 s so the host resubmits.

incidents.title: A soft reset leaves the USB controller running
incidents.seen: about one RAM boot in six came back with no USB until a power cycle.
incidents.cause: the controller and PHY keep their state over a soft reset.
incidents.cause_found_by: measured on the unit
incidents.fix: stop the controller (USBCMD.RS = 0), wait ~50 ms, then reset; 20 of 20 good boots.

incidents.title: Power-on DDR holds garbage (often a NaN)
incidents.seen: a NaN that reached a feedback state (a send effect) silenced the unit until restart.
incidents.cause: DSP DDR is not cleared at power-on; the emulator zero-fills it and hides this.
incidents.cause_found_by: seen on the unit
incidents.fix: never read memory you did not write; fill new DDR with `0xFFFFFFFF` in tests.

incidents.title: A second application on the port corrupts SysEx replies
incidents.seen: with Overbridge holding the port replies were cut at exactly 885 bytes; with Transfer open a preset list showed 35 of 256.
incidents.cause: two clients share the USB MIDI port.
incidents.cause_found_by: seen on the unit
incidents.fix: close Transfer, Overbridge and DNX before a client run; check reply lengths.

incidents.title: A 1024-byte bulk IN transfer wedged the Digitone II's USB controller
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.12 (digikit core/usb-bulk, a vendor bulk interface added in USB MIDI mode), 2026-11-11; the Digitakt II 1.17 ran the fixed adapter the same day
incidents.seen: echo transfers of 1, 511, 512 and 513 bytes worked; 1,024 and 4,096 bytes got no reply, then every bulk send failed and SysEx stopped answering too. The CPU kept running (keys, audio), no crash record was written, and unplugging USB did not bring it back: only a power cycle did.
incidents.cause: the controller has a 64-byte transmit buffer per endpoint. Two back-to-back 512-byte IN packets wedged it the moment the host read them; OUT with two 512-byte packets was fine. Stock does the same thing on purpose: it declares its MIDI IN endpoint as bulk 512 but programs the queue head for 64-byte packets (caps `0x20400000`), as in its audio and Overbridge modes. A first guess (dTD page pointers) was not the cause.
incidents.cause_found_by: bisected on the unit, then read in the controller's reference manual
incidents.fix: the bulk IN queue head is programmed for 64-byte packets while the descriptor keeps 512; the host reads short packets until a frame is complete. Echo then matched from 1 byte to 1 MiB at about 2.3 MB/s each way (DN2) and 2.9 MB/s (DT2), and the emulator now faults an IN transfer whose packets after the first exceed 64 bytes.

incidents.title: Byte-wise reads of uncached DMA buffers stalled the sequencer
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.12 (Digiwerk UM01, multichannel USB audio), 2026-10-31
incidents.seen: 42 channels arrived on the Mac, but the sequencer lagged until unusable.
incidents.cause: the main OS sets CACR `0xa50ce100` / ACR0 `0x4007e020` (`0x40000000-0x47ffffff` cached); the SSI DMA buffers at `0x4e6e7100` are uncached, and UM01 packed their slots with byte-wise reads. A first look at the bootstrap's CACR (cache off) gave a wrong conclusion.
incidents.cause_found_by: read from the start-up code, confirmed by the fixed build on the unit
incidents.fix: read each of the 14 SSI slots once as a 32-bit word (UM02): no lag with busy sequences.

incidents.title: Uncached state in a chord oscillator slowed the UI and could crash the unit
incidents.seen: UI slowed; the unit could crash.
incidents.cause: only `0x40000000-0x43ffffff` is cached; mod state beside the effect delay lines (`0x468xxxxx`) was uncached; ~1,000 accesses per block per voice.
incidents.cause_found_by: read from ACR0, measured by the fix
incidents.fix: copy state to the stack once per block, work there, write it back.

incidents.title: A sample-machine mod could not create the storage it needed
incidents.seen: on units that never had it: 0 % free / 0 bytes in Transfer, stalled uploads, "Connection failed".
incidents.cause: R012 mounts an existing sample filesystem but does not create one; stock FORMAT +DRIVE and the resets do not create it.
incidents.cause_found_by: found by new users; the author's unit had storage prepared during development
incidents.fix: R013 adds SYSTEM > FORMAT SAMPLES; formatting, Transfer capacity (~20 GB) and uploads passed on the unit.

incidents.title: USB audio repeated old audio after a project change
incidents.seen: USB audio froze or repeated while headphones and UI kept working; rejected publications rose by 16,392 in ~10.9 s.
incidents.cause: the TX selector follows RX completion and is no ownership grant; the build bound its queue head to a destination from an older phase.
incidents.cause_found_by: measured with the build's counters
incidents.fix: R011 picks the candidate from the current DMA START.

incidents.title: DAG registers stored through their own DAG hung the DSP
incidents.unit: Digitakt II (PLAITS RINGS kernel, digitakt-ii-research All-in-One)
incidents.seen: the DSP hung on the first block; all audio died. The emulator ran it bit-exactly.
incidents.cause: `DM(I7, M7) = M4` and similar; the PRM forbids it and stock never does it.
incidents.cause_found_by: one-variable probe image on the unit
incidents.fix: move DAG registers through an R register.
incidents.status: fixed; the encoding gate now refuses same-DAG stores.

incidents.title: A frequency shifter froze the unit at boot
incidents.seen: frozen at boot; the emulator showed nothing.
incidents.cause: a selas defect left a nested hardware-loop end compressed; code copied into L2 at run time was not written back from the data cache.
incidents.cause_found_by: two causes, isolated on the unit
incidents.fix: `.NOCOMPRESS` around nested loops; cache write-back before running copied code. Ran on send and master 2026-10-30.

incidents.title: A decoded section 7 over 1 MiB crashed the unit
incidents.seen: crash; recovered over the startup menu.
incidents.cause: the ColdFire depacks section 7 into a 1 MiB buffer and checks the size only afterwards.
incidents.cause_found_by: read from the loader
incidents.fix: keep the decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes.

incidents.title: Per-sample stores to the DDR output buffer crashed the unit
incidents.seen: continuous tone, unit crashed; the emulator was bit-identical.
incidents.cause: per-sample accesses to stock buffers in external DDR (`0x8045b3c0`).
incidents.cause_found_by: measured on the unit
incidents.fix: render into L2 and copy once per block.

incidents.title: The flash cave reportedly froze a unit at the logo
incidents.seen: one report of a freeze at the logo with code in the cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000`; other projects boot from the same cave on units.
incidents.cause: not settled ([CONFLICTS O18](CONFLICTS.md)).
incidents.fix: check the bytes the other cave users leave; prove the cave on a hard run.

incidents.title: Patching a "free" zero run crashed the unit
incidents.seen: crash; the emulator watch read zeros there.
incidents.cause: the run was an array that the code fills at run time.
incidents.cause_found_by: found by a run-time watch and static analysis
incidents.fix: two static checks (equal-stride gaps, referenced operands); only 13 runs (4,207 B) pass both.

incidents.title: Mod code at a "free" address crashed projects with certain samples
incidents.seen: projects with SP TWINSHOT samples crashed at boot.
incidents.cause: mod code at `0x46000000`, memory stock uses for those samples.
incidents.fix: v0.8.1 unpacks the mod code into a 64 KB block that a hook at the end of heap init (`0x4010358E`) reserves first.

incidents.title: MD and Monomachine tracks went silent after an install
incidents.seen: intermittent: tracks silent until cleared.
incidents.cause: unknown (suspected stale voice-slot state or state from an older version's project).
incidents.fix: none yet; test an old project after every install.

incidents.title: A mod broke the normal USB update path
incidents.seen: the next OS sent with Transfer stopped at "Receiving" or "PREPARING..." and wrote nothing.
incidents.cause: the mod's build; fixed in 1.0.1.
incidents.fix: the STARTUP menu over DIN (~15 min); a release test that installs the next build over USB.

incidents.title: Plaits builds failed normal Transfer updates at PREPARING
incidents.unit: Digitakt II (digitakt-ii-research All-in-One, earlier Plaits builds)
incidents.seen: updates stopped at 0 % / PREPARING.
incidents.cause: not stated; the author says not to assume the route is reliable everywhere.
incidents.fix: power cycle and the startup menu.

incidents.title: A granular engine froze the UI at low pitch
incidents.seen: UI froze at low pitch.
incidents.cause: fixed-length source grains became long, the pool filled and every voice ran its worst case.
incidents.fix: grain length independent of pitch; overlap capped.

incidents.title: Clobbering R8 at the FX-bus mixer hook lost all audio
incidents.seen: no audio; the emulator ignored the stray state.
incidents.cause: the mixer takes R4 and R8 as arguments; the hook changed R8.
incidents.fix: preserve every register and flag that code after a hook reads; compare callee registers between stock and the build.

incidents.title: A boot block of 8n+4 bytes left the unit silent
incidents.seen: silent from power-on; boots in the emulator.
incidents.cause: the L2 instruction-cache line fill over the block's end faults on ECC.
incidents.fix: whole 32-byte boot blocks (`dspblocks.pad_lines`, `bootblocks.py`).

incidents.title: An encoding every decoder accepts raised ILOPI on the chip
incidents.seen: the unit stopped (illegal opcode).
incidents.cause: negative shift immediates with zero sign bits in the middle parcel (stock: `023e 7800`); selas's 48-bit `Rn = <sysreg>` put the wrong register (EMUCLK read as LCNTR).
incidents.cause_found_by: decoded against stock
incidents.fix: stock encodings only; compressed forms for system registers; check the disassembly.

incidents.title: A select value outside its count stalled the sequencer
incidents.seen: after a build changed an effect's parameter layout, an old project stalled the sequencer on first play.
incidents.cause: stored values no longer fit the new layout.
incidents.fix: stamp old projects' stored values after a layout change.

incidents.title: DSP scratch at `$84` and up hung the unit
incidents.seen: hang.
incidents.cause: r7 scratch `$00-$83` is the per-instance block; above it belongs to others.
incidents.fix: stay inside the per-instance block.

incidents.title: Key events posted into stock's queues crashed the unit minutes later
incidents.seen: two crashes, minutes after the event.
incidents.cause: events posted straight into stock's internal queues.
incidents.fix: feed the panel parser its own bytes instead.

incidents.title: Restoring DSP-read state every frame corrupted the audio
incidents.seen: corrupted audio.
incidents.cause: a mod overwrote data the DSP reads each frame; doing so is safe only for CPU-side bookkeeping.
incidents.fix: restore only CPU-side state.

incidents.title: A DSP frame counter saturated after 50.7 minutes
incidents.seen: a frame engine stopped after 50.7 minutes.
incidents.cause: a counter past `$7fffff` saturates in `move a,nN`.
incidents.fix: mask counters to 23 bits.

incidents.title: Module state on a load-meter counter gave a jittery pitch
incidents.seen: jittery pitch.
incidents.cause: module state at `X:$2840`, core 1's load-meter counter.
incidents.fix: move the state.

incidents.title: A startup change stalled at the logo after a long power-off
incidents.seen: passed emulator boots and quick power cycles, stalled at the logo after several minutes off.
incidents.cause: unknown; keeping the activation helper resident fixed it.
incidents.fix: qualify startup changes after a long power-off.

incidents.title: USB replies stayed stale for minutes
incidents.seen: a value the CPU stores rarely stayed stale in USB replies; values stored every frame looked live.
incidents.cause: DMA reads RAM, not the copyback cache.
incidents.cause_found_by: measured
incidents.fix: copy a reply through the uncached alias and send it from there.

incidents.title: A menu table in a "free" zero run crashed the unit
incidents.seen: crash.
incidents.cause: the 15 KB zero run at `0x401087e4` lies in the PROJECT subsystem's RAM (the zero region above `0x400d8000`).
incidents.fix: larger code goes to a loader-copied area (octabam's loader stub at `0x4010fdf0`).

incidents.title: Idle paths of sixteen mods cost two percent of a Rytm block
incidents.unit: Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74 (Modwerk library, 16-module set, sequencer stopped), 2026-11-06
incidents.seen: the idle audio block took 72.9 % with the set installed.
incidents.cause: three modules did work every block with nothing to do: Ping Pong Loop's four voice gates called the mirror routine for every voice in stock's sample prefetch, Sample Playback Rate walked all eight voices, QPERF ran its handler in full.
incidents.cause_found_by: measured on the unit, block timed on DTIM0 over USB MIDI
incidents.fix: early returns when idle (a byte of armed voices, "no track has RATE on"): 70.6-71.1 %.
incidents.status: fixed in the pinned packages; not run alone on a unit.

incidents.title: Mod data written for default settings slowed project load and save
incidents.seen: a user saw a project load slowly when switched to from another project, and a slower save; a reboot straight into it loaded normally.
incidents.cause: the ARP mod sealed a 320-byte carrier for every kit even with default settings, so load checked all 1,664 bindings; the project itself was valid.
incidents.cause_found_by: shown in the emulator on the user's export
incidents.fix: leave the carrier absent while all thirteen rows are defaults: 81 % fewer emulated instructions for a full serialization.
incidents.status: fixed offline; wall-clock times on the unit not measured yet.

incidents.title: The sample popup did not open after switching Machines
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11 (armio; R020 last confirmed installation), 2026-11-06
incidents.seen: after selecting ONESHOT, turning knob D did not open the sample list.
incidents.cause: the separate sampler SYN view was not selected when the Machine changed within the audio-track class. Generic notifications redrew the old stock view. Earlier tests manually reselected SYN and hid the missing lifecycle transition. No live capture established that every intermittent popup report shares this cause.
incidents.cause_found_by: native replay
incidents.fix: R021 defers reconciliation to the existing UI poll, uses native selection and ownership, and avoids modal/selected-trig transitions; included in R022.
incidents.status: ten native transitions and nine guard cases passed; hardware confirmation pending.

incidents.title: New project samples were missing after reboot
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11 (armio; report build unconfirmed, exact R020 reproduced), 2026-11-06
incidents.seen: newly loaded samples disappeared from the unsaved working project after a freeze and reboot. Deletion of the +Drive sample files was not established.
incidents.cause: load notification ran the native incremental settings serializer, but the port updated its sample companion only during whole-project serialization. Both prepared working backup and fresh emulated boot retained an empty identity for the loaded slot. The frozen device's actual backup state was not captured.
incidents.cause_found_by: native replay
incidents.fix: R022 refreshes the working sample companion in that settings worker under the existing project lock, validates owner/UID, and preserves explicit saved checkpoints.
incidents.status: load, unload, fresh-emulator restore, saved-cache isolation and invalid-state guards passed. Physical reboot confirmation is pending; a frozen worker or interrupted write can still lose pending work. The USB freeze is unresolved.

incidents.title: A knob's own push-button byte was read as FUNC
incidents.unit: Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74 (Modwerk, Improved Machine Browser build MBC2), 2026-11-08
incidents.seen: FUNC + knob turn in the machine list behaved like a plain turn.
incidents.cause: the module took byte +20 of the encoder event as FUNC; that byte is set while the knob's own push-button is held.
incidents.cause_found_by: found from the tester's unit report, then the code
incidents.fix: build MBC3 reads FUNC from the stock key table.
incidents.status: fixed; MBC3 passed on the unit.

incidents.title: A demand-loader soak froze an Octatrack MKII
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C (octabam images OCTABAMS4 and OCTABAMS5, both with STEM REC), 2026-11-08/09
incidents.seen: 8 Nov: the DSP frame count stopped in 3 of 19 effect switches during play; panel and MIDI still answered, a power cycle was needed. 9 Nov: OCTABAMS5 froze once in 118 switches with panel, audio and USB all stopped.
incidents.cause: the demand loader's BASE/MODULATION transition is the larger factor (only the loader changed between the two images, and the rate fell from about 1 in 6 to 1 in 118); STEM REC and its 18 MiB reserve are not cleared. Candidate for the total freeze: two waits in the frame interrupt with no time limit (the loader's wait before each host word, and stock's spin until the DSP takes the frame's host command).
incidents.cause_found_by: open; found by a scripted program-change soak with the load meter and loader diagnostics polled over USB
incidents.fix: partial (one copy per load). Time limits on the waits and copying a slice per frame are proposed, not made.

incidents.title: A wavetable machine clicked on every note
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C (octabam WAVE as a ColdFire machine, builds W1-W5), 2026-11-07
incidents.seen: a click on every note.
incidents.cause: the DSP's AMP envelope restarts from zero at every trig START; with any ATK above 0 a sound that keeps playing across trigs drops to silence and fades back in.
incidents.cause_found_by: heard on the unit, then traced under the port
incidents.fix: hold the DSP at ATK 0 / HOLD INF / REL INF and shape AMP in the machine, as SYNTH MACHINE does (W5).
incidents.status: fixed from W5. The module README still says "not flashed" (CONFLICTS O22).

incidents.title: Patch state inside a stock task's buffer silenced tracks
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C (OCTAMAX up to 2g), fixed 2026-11-09
incidents.seen: tracks went silent or sounded wrong, scene A showed nothing selected after a pattern change, once `EXCEPTION VEC:03` at the stock key dispatcher's return. Not reproducible on demand.
incidents.cause: patch state at `0x80006a00-0x80007000` lay inside the work buffer of the stock audio-analysis task (`0x80006964-0x80007574`). The crash is not proven to come from this.
incidents.cause_found_by: read from the code
incidents.fix: OCTAMAX_2h keeps all patch state in DDR; the build refuses any operand that points into the buffer.
incidents.status: fixed, confirmed on the unit 2026-11-09; the crash cause stays open.

incidents.title: A long copy with interrupts masked clicked on every reload
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI (KYOTI V1.7 work build, RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT), 2026-11-09
incidents.seen: a click on every [PTN] + [BANK] + trig reload.
incidents.cause: a 43 KB pattern copy ran with interrupts masked and held off the audio frame.
incidents.cause_found_by: found from the user's report
incidents.fix: copy with interrupts on and publish only the slices that changed. Also fixed in the same round: reloading the current pattern while another was cued let the cued one land anyway.

incidents.title: A safe-boot trial crashed every boot
incidents.seen: after the first bank was written and the unit restarted, `EXCEPTION DK0094 V03` (address error) at every startup.
incidents.cause: the boot's eMMC accessor table had no write function, so marking the bank TRYING called address 0; the record never changed, so every boot retried the same bank. The unit tests had replaced exactly this piece with doubles.
incidents.cause_found_by: from the exception screen's words, then the code
incidents.fix: core 1.7.1 adds the write function, storage fails closed on a table without one, and an end-to-end test through the production loader reproduces the crash.
incidents.status: fixed in code; the physical rollback test is pending, and the recovery steps used are not stated.

incidents.title: A mod's memory window broke the BASE/WDTH filter
incidents.seen: moving BASE gave artifacts and some tracks went silent.
incidents.cause: the stock base-width filter reads Q31 poles from a 508-entry table with a zero tail and indexes up to 1023; Synfact's companion window sat in that tail, so BASE+WDTH of 128 or more read code as poles.
incidents.cause_found_by: shown in the emulator
incidents.fix: core 1.7.2 bounds the index to 508.

incidents.title: A chorus running from DDR overloaded the Syntakt's MAIN CPU
incidents.seen: MAIN at 100 % and the sound broke up.
incidents.cause: all chorus code ran from DDR; about 5.4 KB of code was fetched per block.
incidents.cause_found_by: measured on the unit
incidents.fix: 0.2 moved the hot code and kernels into MAIN SRAM (0.2 KB fetched per block).

incidents.title: A machine kind past the end of a label table froze Digitone II units
incidents.seen: the unit froze on MACHINE SEL > BOUNCE, and at every power-on of a project holding a BOUNCE track.
incidents.cause: the label lookup picked the Monomachine label table by range; BOUNCE (kind 13) read past its end and walked address `0xEE` as a list. The emulator reads low memory as zeros, which hid it (I66 has the gate side).
incidents.cause_found_by: from a user's freeze report, then traced
incidents.fix: one explicit test per machine kind, a `machines` gate step, and a trap on any non-stock read below `0x40000000` in every emulator step (v0.45). Recovery used: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 2 (EMPTY RESET; the +Drive is kept), then flash v0.45.

incidents.title: A mod took stock's USB DISK MODE pause for a DSP stall and kept the audio off
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI and MKII, OS 1.40C (Modwerk beta base; finding 72, several testers' units), late Oct to 2026-11-10
incidents.seen: after walking PROJECT > SYSTEM into USB DISK MODE (or OS UPGRADE) and backing out, the unit stayed silent until a power cycle; the base's records said the DSPs had stopped.
incidents.cause: stock pauses the DSP while USB DISK MODE is open. The base's stall watch read that pause as a stalled DSP, and its recovery held the audio stopped. It was never reproduced on a stock unit.
incidents.fix: the base tells that pause from a stall (2026-11-10); on the owner's MKII the walk, about 10 s in the mode, NO and PLAY now plays.
incidents.status: fixed on the live base; a flashed base, file copies in the mode and an OS upgrade from the card not yet tested.

incidents.title: Spring-reverb builds lost their sound on a Digitone II; no cause found offline
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.12 (naturarum's Digiwerk / dn2-cfw, spring builds EFES and EEES), 2026-11-04 to 11-08
incidents.seen: EFES locked three times on Digiwerk 0.4 (twice in a short session, once after about 50 minutes; no sound on PLAY, the synths silent), always on USB MULTI/MIDI. EEES, the spring alone, stopped the sound for good one or two minutes after a pattern stop and in OS UPGRADE. A build with a -240 dB floor in the spring was silent from power-on. CFTE without the spring ran an hour and 30 minutes on the same USB mode without a lock.
incidents.cause: not found. An offline search ruled out illegal instructions and accesses, parity, FP exceptions, the stack, Elektron's code, timing in digikit's coupled emulator, and digikit's SHARC+ silicon rules (checked on every build, no hit). The one lead: the spring's output is exactly 0 from 1.4 s into FX kill and 78 s after a stop, as at both unit stops [inferred].
incidents.fix: the spring is shelved; its six builds stay withdrawn. The author stopped blind device tests. The next test build (EEEM, a light morphing reverb in the reverb slot) sends the stock DSP's idle parks to a fault tone whose pitch names the fault (1500 Hz illegal instruction, 3000 Hz parity, 6000 Hz emulation or default handler, 1500 + 6000 Hz abort or stack check; a ~750 Hz buzz or silence is a hang).
incidents.status: open; EEEM not yet on the unit (2026-11-10).

incidents.title: A DSP load guard dropped a sample voice block after block
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11 (dn2mk2 v0.47, a user's unit), reported 2026-11-10
incidents.seen: with a SID voice and three PERC tracks playing, an ONESHOT kick sounded crunchy at about 85 % DSP load.
incidents.cause: the frame-time guard left the sample voice out when a block ran short of time, and because a sample voice is retried in every block it came and went block by block instead of stopping.
incidents.cause_found_by: from the report and the guard's code
incidents.fix: planned for v0.49: render the sample voices first, so time runs out on the heavy synth voices, and keep a dropped sample voice stopped until its next note, as PERC voices already are.

incidents.title: A drum machine mod played silent hits after power-up and misread stock's voice start
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C (octabam's DRUMMER by djib, the author's unit, images 44-46), 2026-11-05/06
incidents.seen: the machine, its kit window and AUTO kit worked, but hits stayed silent until the machine was chosen again or the track's audio editor was touched; retrigs did not run.
incidents.cause: the hit level was scaled from a base read only when a restore bit at `0x80001538` was clear, and on the unit that bit can be set at power-up, so the base stayed 0. Separately, the mod's wrapper of the FLEX voice start passed two arguments where stock's routine `0x4000f450(track, slot, flags)` takes three, so stock read a word of the wrapper's stack.
incidents.cause_found_by: found under octabam's emulator after the unit test
incidents.fix: the base is now the lane's VOL; the wrapper forwards all three arguments, and stock's retrigs run.
incidents.status: fixed; later images (to 78, 2026-11-09) ran on the author's MKII.

incidents.title: The emulator undercounted DSP time by 2x to 12x
incidents.unit: Digitakt II (70b185's project; digimod's Plaits mod)
incidents.seen: device cycles about 2x the emulator's instruction count for code reading DDR; a hard stop the emulator showed overshooting by ~25k overshot by ~75k on the unit; digimod reports 7-12x on hardware for one case.
incidents.cause: the emulators model no memory stalls.
incidents.fix: budget with silicon costs; leave a margin; measure once per project on the unit.

incidents.title: A SHARC emulator shifted every fractional multiply
incidents.seen: found when the emulator was checked against stock routines.
incidents.cause: the emulator shifted every fractional multiply left; the PRM shifts only signed x signed.
incidents.fix: fixed in the emulator; `sharc_checks.py` calls stock routines and compares.

incidents.title: Low-window flash pointers boot in the emulator and hang on the unit
incidents.seen: images boot in the emulator and hang on the unit.
incidents.cause: after the OS remaps CS0, nothing decodes the low window on hardware; the emulator maps flash at `0x0` and `0x10000000`.
incidents.fix: link and point through `0x10000000`; scan images for low pointers.

incidents.title: The default compression level corrupted a DN2 image
incidents.seen: corrupt image.
incidents.cause: section 4's in-place loader has a stock margin of +31,182 bytes; elektron-firmware-tool's `-l 3` gives -39,318. Stock DT2 1.17 also fails the in-place path (margin -31,912).
incidents.fix: check the margin at every loader stage; a dense packer.

incidents.title: A "no change" rebuild came out 2 bytes short
incidents.seen: the null repack failed.
incidents.cause: elektron-firmware-tool padded ELE2 containers to 2 bytes; stock pads to 4.
incidents.fix: pad to 4; always null-repack the stock file first.

incidents.title: A label defined twice resolved to the wrong file
incidents.unit: Digitakt II (Plaits kernels, caught before a unit)
incidents.seen: each kernel's own test passed; the merged image jumped into the wrong file.
incidents.cause: a label defined in two sources resolves to one of them in the merged object.
incidents.fix: unique label prefixes per file.

incidents.title: Checks reported success about work they never did
incidents.seen: the build passed every check and faulted on the unit.
incidents.cause: snapshot harnesses cleared code no real boot ran; a boot gate printed "Safe to flash" after its coverage section was deleted; an emulator call returned 0 for a present value.
incidents.fix: every check gets a control that must fail.

incidents.title: Boot-screen frames were upright in the emulator and flipped on the panel
incidents.seen: a boot screen whose bar was at the bottom in the preview and the emulator appeared at the top on the panel; left-to-right fill was unchanged.
incidents.cause: the emulator decodes the intro bitmap as if the intro flush flipped like the main-UI blit. On the panel, intro rows are stored top-down mirrored. Why the intro path differs (flush routine or panel scan direction) is not established.
incidents.cause_found_by: shown on the unit, plus a comparison of the stock logo with the bootloader picture: 0 mismatching pixels after a vertical flip
incidents.fix: digikit's `.dkbs` frames, safe screen and pixel helper use the panel's layout. The emulator decoder is not fixed yet.
incidents.status: worked around; emulator still wrong for intro frames.

incidents.title: A test plan pressed the wrong key, and the emulator reference did not match the unit
incidents.unit: Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74 (Modwerk, Kit A/B runs KBH7 and KBH8), 2026-11-08/09
incidents.seen: two runs tested only the KIT-menu path; another run stopped because the unit's kit list draws markers after kits 02-16 that the emulator's reference image lacks.
incidents.cause: rytm2_mods' documentation gives the reload key as NO + PLAY, so the remote-key plan pressed transport PLAY; the OS 1.74 manual says NO + PLAY MODE.
incidents.cause_found_by: caught in review
incidents.fix: rerun with NO + PLAY MODE and narrow the screen check to the cursor row.

incidents.title: Odd jump targets froze a Digitakt II at boot; the emulator kept running
incidents.seen: the unit froze at boot.
incidents.cause: byte-aligned code sections put routines at odd addresses; a jsr/jmp to an odd address stops the ColdFire with an address error (vector 3), while the emulator keeps running.
incidents.cause_found_by: per the fix's commit message
incidents.fix: the linker refuses an odd-target absolute jsr/jmp into mod RAM; each code section starts with a 2-byte alignment.

incidents.title: Code built into .bss crashed a Digitakt II at boot; the emulator ran the zeros
incidents.unit: Digitakt II, OS 1.17 (gdeo607's Digi2Core, core-dt2 2.4-2.6), fixed in 2.6.1 on 2026-11-09
incidents.seen: right after boot the unit stopped with an illegal-instruction exception.
incidents.cause: two new routines were placed in `.bss` instead of the code section, so the unit jumped into zero-filled memory. The emulator executed the zeros as no-ops and booted.
incidents.cause_found_by: per the 2.6.1 note
incidents.fix: the routines are code again in 2.6.1. The README says not to flash a 2.4, 2.5 or 2.6 build; Digi2MacroOSC and Digi2ElixirPotionsDRUM still name core 2.4.

incidents.title: A feature that crosses ColdFire and DSP passed the gate and failed on units
incidents.seen: on testers' units BOUNCE recorded nothing, or recorded and never played back.
incidents.cause: unknown. The gate never ran the ColdFire and the DSP together. Per the v0.48 notes the recorder trigs fired and takes were made, but the track never played its buffer.
incidents.fix: BOUNCE removed from the menu in v0.47 and its code removed in v0.48 (old projects load, the track silent). v0.48 adds a coupled emulator that runs both processors one audio block at a time (faithful in order and content, not in timing margins) and the first gate step on it; FLEX, the replacement, is to be tested from recording to playback on it.

incidents.title: Recovery stalled at ~80 %: the MIDI link, not the image
incidents.seen: Transfer showed 100 % sent; the unit's bar froze near 80 % (30/70/80 % on different tries).
incidents.cause: a USB MIDI interface went idle mid-transfer and dropped packets.
incidents.cause_found_by: shown by sending stock 1.10E over the same route
incidents.fix: a MIDI interface that stays awake for the ~12-15 min transfer.

incidents.title: Recovery used on a Digitakt II after a crashing build; a cheap cable delivered nothing
incidents.seen: startup menu over DIN restored 1.16; a generic USB-MIDI cable (VID 1a86, PID 752d) showed no reception, a known-good interface worked.
incidents.cause: the cable.
incidents.fix: rehearse recovery with your exact cable and the stock file.

incidents.title: Recovery used on a Digitone MK1 after a logo hang
incidents.seen: a build hung on the logo; stock 1.44 restored over the startup menu and DIN.
incidents.cause: the build.
incidents.fix: startup menu; not EMPTY RESET or FACTORY RESET.

incidents.title: Syntakt startup-menu recovery tested over DIN
incidents.seen: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, stock 1.42 from Transfer's legacy SysEx page through a generic USB-to-MIDI cable: the unit booted 1.42. A working unit; a unit that does not boot is untested.
incidents.cause: test.

incidents.title: Stock storage resets did not create the sample filesystem
incidents.seen: per the author, FORMAT +DRIVE, EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET do not create the sample filesystem and can erase projects.
incidents.cause: stock has no such filesystem on the DN2.
incidents.fix: the mod's own FORMAT SAMPLES (R013).

incidents.title: Safe mode by REC at power-on, tested on a Digitakt II
incidents.unit: Digitakt II, OS 1.17 (digikit, branch image with loadable boot screens), 2026-11-08
incidents.seen: REC held from power-on gave digikit's safe mode (no modules loaded; the DIGIKIT menu showed "safe mode key held"). Without REC, the selected boot screen played about 1.8 s after the stock intro started, and the module setting survived power cycles.
incidents.cause: test. In the emulator, digikit's earlier queue scan missed the key (`safe:0`); reading the stock key state fixed it. On the unit, a key held at power-on does produce a report.
incidents.status: tested on one DT2. Other panel firmware versions and the Digitone II are not measured. A fault during the intro still reaches stock's halting handler; the 30 s boot counter, not REC, catches that (emulator only).

stock_bugs.title: eMMC TRIM fails with TRIM ERROR on a busy card
stock_bugs.symptom: TRIM ERROR at a sector number; after a restart at another one.
stock_bugs.trigger: many TRIMs in a row while the card is busy (seen while a mod erased its own data).
stock_bugs.cause: the busy wait after CMD38 arms the DAT0 edge interrupt before it tests DAT0, leaving a stale semaphore post; the next TRIM on a busy card returns at once and the call after it gets no answer. The driver has no timeout.
stock_bugs.workaround: read `PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024` before every TRIM and verify read, call only when idle; retry (TRIM is idempotent); fixed in dn2mk2 v0.40.
stock_bugs.test_tip: a mod that erases or rewrites many blocks must be tested on a card that is busy, not only on an idle one.
stock_bugs.found_by: dn2mk2 (error seen on a unit; cause read from stock code)

stock_bugs.title: Song LOAD trusts a stored row count and halts the unit
stock_bugs.symptom: a project halts the instrument when opened, on stock and modded builds alike.
stock_bugs.trigger: a song whose stored row count is out of range (one project held 21,503 rows, at most 99 are valid).
stock_bugs.cause: song LOAD `0x400dea6a` reads the count as a signed word at stored `+2891` and copies that many 29-byte rows into 37-byte live rows without a check.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by the `songguard` mod (dn2_firmware_explore, also in dn2mk2): a damaged song loads empty; confirmed on hardware. Users: repair the project (row count at record `+0x147`).
stock_bugs.test_tip: a project that crashes your build may crash stock too: open it on stock before you debug your mod.
stock_bugs.found_by: dn2_firmware_explore (seen on a unit, cause read from stock code)
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: The USB upgrade receiver does not check the 2 MiB limit
stock_bugs.symptom: an oversized image stalls at the end of the transfer; nothing is written; a power cycle clears it.
stock_bugs.cause: a 2 MiB receive buffer without a size check.
stock_bugs.workaround: keep the container under 2 MiB; check the size in the build.
stock_bugs.test_tip: a build that "hangs while updating" may just be too big.

stock_bugs.title: Auto-commit upload loses its "upload complete" event
stock_bugs.symptom: the unit sits on "OS UPGRADE / Receiving".
stock_bugs.trigger: the first auto-commit upload after boot, sent before the upgrade view is open.
stock_bugs.cause: the OS posts "upload complete" while the view is not open; the event is lost.
stock_bugs.workaround: upload without auto-commit, then send End(1), which checks the bytes and posts the event itself.
stock_bugs.test_tip: a flashing script that hangs once and works the second time may be meeting this.
stock_bugs.found_by: complex-ping's Digitone II modding skill (seen on a unit, read from stock code)

stock_bugs.title: LFO TRIG MODE ONE and HALF do not run one (half) cycle and hold
stock_bugs.symptom: with TRIG MODE ONE or HALF the LFO does not run exactly one cycle (half a cycle) from its start phase and then hold the value it reached; two separate stock bugs, on audio and MIDI tracks.
stock_bugs.trigger: set an LFO's TRIG MODE to ONE or HALF and trigger it.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by the `lfolength` mod (dn2_firmware_explore; supersedes `lfohold`); confirmed on hardware on an audio track (2026-10-09), MIDI tracks in the emulator.
stock_bugs.test_tip: do not judge an LFO mod by ONE/HALF behaviour without comparing stock.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: The stock restart does not wait for the +Drive or drain the panel link
stock_bugs.symptom: a restart triggered by code can cut off a +Drive write or a panel message in flight.
stock_bugs.trigger: calling stock's own restart from a mod while the card or the panel link is busy.
stock_bugs.cause: stock's restart does not wait for the +Drive and does not let the panel link drain with interrupts on.
stock_bugs.workaround: elekloader core-dn1 exports `core_restart`, which does both; use it instead of stock's.
stock_bugs.test_tip: a mod that restarts the unit should be tested right after a save and while keys are pressed.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; worked around by a core

stock_bugs.title: EP0 data stages of a multiple of 64 bytes stall or freeze
stock_bugs.symptom: the request after a 64/128/192/256-byte reply returns 0 bytes; once the unit froze; 128/192-byte OUT stages never complete.
stock_bugs.trigger: a control transfer whose data stage is a multiple of 64 bytes.
stock_bugs.cause: stock leaves zero-length termination on in the EP0 OUT queue head.
stock_bugs.workaround: size replies a byte short, or clear ZLT when priming.
stock_bugs.test_tip: test USB replies of exactly 64 and 128 bytes on purpose.

stock_bugs.title: About one EP0 OUT stage in 50-100 goes unanswered
stock_bugs.symptom: host requests time out now and then.
stock_bugs.trigger: many EP0 OUT stages in a row.
stock_bugs.cause: the stage completes inside the ISR after stock's poll, or stops part-way.
stock_bugs.workaround: finish a completed stage from a 60 Hz tick, or stall EP0 after 0.5 s so the host resubmits.
stock_bugs.test_tip: count timeouts over a thousand requests, not ten.

stock_bugs.title: A Plays-Free MIDI track stalls after its first step
stock_bugs.symptom: the track stops after its first step on a manual trig.
stock_bugs.trigger: a Plays-Free MIDI track with trig quantize Direct and pattern scale Per Track, triggered manually.
stock_bugs.cause: read from stock code at `0x4009b6f2` (an 18-byte splice fixes it).
stock_bugs.test_tip: a sequencer mod that uses scales Per Track can run into this on stock paths.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: A pattern that holds only parameter locks shows as empty
stock_bugs.symptom: the pattern's grid LED stays unlit under [PTN], as for an unused slot.
stock_bugs.trigger: a pattern whose only content is parameter locks (on a MIDI track, or trigless locks on an audio track), with no trig.
stock_bugs.cause: stock's "used" test looks at trigs only.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by BATCH_BUGFIXES (`EMPTY_PATTERN_LED_FIX`) under [PTN]; under [BANK] it stays as stock, because scanning 256 patterns' locks on every LED refresh starved the CPU.
stock_bugs.test_tip: do not overwrite a "free" pattern slot in a test project without checking for locks.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: A pattern-triggered Part change carries the old Part's state over
stock_bugs.symptom: a track leaving PICKUP for FLEX keeps playing the old Part's pickup loop; the recorder's SRC/RLEN cache goes stale; a pattern switch into a PICKUP track marks the Part edited when nothing changed. Also reported on Elektronauts.
stock_bugs.trigger: a pattern change that changes Part, with a track going from PICKUP to another machine.
stock_bugs.cause: the "select Part" handler `0x400621a6` calls `FUN_400972fc` per track, whose PICKUP-to-other branch does nothing; PICKUP and FLEX share one sample arena, so the stale pointer still looks valid; nothing republishes the recorder cache.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by BATCH_BUGFIXES (`PART_CHANGE_CARRYOVER_FIX`): republish the recorder records, set the voice-kill bit, re-seed the slot.
stock_bugs.test_tip: a mod that changes Parts (DIRECT JUMP and others) reaches the same stock path and shows the same symptom; compare a stock pattern change.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: A trigless lock stays lit after its last lock is erased
stock_bugs.symptom: the step stays lit on the trig row forever, although it is now inert.
stock_bugs.trigger: erase the last remaining lock of a trigless lock.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by octatrack-kyoti-fw's ERASE_EMPTY_TRIGLESS_LOCKS (a deliberately empty trigless lock placed with FUNC + TRIG is left alone).
stock_bugs.test_tip: lit steps after a lock edit are not necessarily your mod.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: LO-FI's AMF ring-mod pitch falls at eleven values instead of rising
stock_bugs.device_os: Octatrack MKI and MKII, OS 1.40C (LO-FI on FX1 and FX2)
stock_bugs.symptom: turning AMF up lowers the ring-mod pitch at AMF 8, 17, 23, 28, 32, 35, 37, 40, 42, 45 and 48 (worst at 7 to 8, about 63 % lower); monotonic again above 48.
stock_bugs.trigger: LO-FI with AMF in those ranges (also reached by LFOs, scenes and fine values).
stock_bugs.cause: the coefficient's extended-precision multiply starts with `mpysu x0,y0,a` (signed x unsigned) on two magnitudes; when the low word's top bit is set the partial product's sign flips. Reported to Elektron, not fixed upstream.
stock_bugs.workaround: `mpyuu` instead (octa-bt-pt's LOFI AMF FIX; also a Modwerk draft module). Saved projects at affected values will sound different with the fix.
stock_bugs.test_tip: an effect mod that compares against LO-FI by ear may be comparing against this bug.
stock_bugs.found_by: octa-bt-pt (AMF 0-127 x fine 0-127 swept in the DSP emulator with the fix: monotonic)
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod (not yet run on hardware per the Modwerk draft)

stock_bugs.title: Probable: SPATIALIZER's ring misaligns when selected mid-play
stock_bugs.symptom: a misaligned delay ring when SPATIALIZER is selected while playing with a non-zero held offset; later calls can read across the ring end (wet path only); re-selecting at offset 0 realigns.
stock_bugs.cause: the dispatcher splits a frame's FX call at `x:$20c`, and SPATIALIZER's init zeroes its ring write offset between the two calls, misaligning the ring by 32 - 2 x offset.
stock_bugs.workaround: none yet; the source plans a hardware test on stock.
stock_bugs.test_tip: odd SPATIALIZER artefacts after switching effects live may be stock.

stock_bugs.title: The AUDIO EDITOR key opens the sample the track had before
stock_bugs.symptom: after a track copy/paste or a Part reload, the [AUDIO EDITOR] key shows the old sample's name, waveform and slices.
stock_bugs.trigger: change a track's sample by copy/paste or Part reload, then press [AUDIO EDITOR] without reselecting the track.
stock_bugs.cause: stock reuses the sample the track had when it was last selected.
stock_bugs.workaround: reselect the track first; fixed by OCTAMAX 2f.
stock_bugs.test_tip: when a mod changes a track's sample, reselect the track before you judge the editor.
stock_bugs.found_by: OCTAMAX (seen on a unit; fix confirmed on an MKII 2026-11-07)
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: Edits to hidden FX words overwrite the delay's saved TIME (latent)
stock_bugs.symptom: after an edit of live FX words 38-41 and a power cycle, the delay TIME comes back wrong (2 instead of 23 in the test).
stock_bugs.trigger: a parameter setter writes FX words 38-41. The stock UI never edits them, so only mods reach this.
stock_bugs.cause: the FX edit save maps words 38-41 to stored slot 0, which holds the delay's TIME.
stock_bugs.workaround: keep mod values for those words in your own storage (Modwerk's base redirects them to its kit storage).
stock_bugs.test_tip: after any mod that touches FX words, save, power-cycle and check the delay TIME.

stock_bugs.title: A non-sample file on the +Drive hangs LOAD TO PROJECT and later stalls the OS upgrade
stock_bugs.symptom: loading a file that is not a sample (a raw `.elemod` in this case) into the project hangs the unit; a project that holds such a file then stalls the next OS upgrade at PREPARING until CREATE NEW.
stock_bugs.trigger: any file on the +Drive's sample filesystem is listed by SAMPLES, in every folder; LOAD TO PROJECT reads its first 16 bytes as the sample header without a check.
stock_bugs.cause: per elekloader, LOAD TO PROJECT trusts the 16-byte header at the start of the file.
stock_bugs.workaround: a tool that stores other files on the +Drive starts each with 16 zero bytes, which stock loads as an empty sample (elekloader's Drive Loader does this).
stock_bugs.test_tip: keep test files off the +Drive, or give them the zero header; if an OS upgrade stalls at PREPARING after +Drive experiments, try CREATE NEW before blaming the image.

stock_bugs.title: A random exception while browsing (filesystem block cache)
stock_bugs.trigger: browsing (the source gives no exact steps).
stock_bugs.cause: the filesystem block cache, per Model-TG.
stock_bugs.workaround: fixed by Model-TG ("a long-standing stock bug"), and in builds that include it (Modded-Cycles lists it).
stock_bugs.test_tip: an exception while browsing on a modded build is not necessarily the mod.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a mod

stock_bugs.title: Eleven sequencer and UI bugs fixed by ems-monomachine-firmware
stock_bugs.symptom: as listed in the project's changelog: clearing a track in EDIT KIT sets GND>SIN's TUNE to -64 instead of 0; leaving the snapshot manager through the KIT shortcut can make later COPY/PASTE/CLEAR act on snapshots; switching POLY mode on or off during playback can mute tracks when MULTI ENV > SUS is 0; MULTI ENV changes do not persist while POLY mode is active; notes in POLY mode get stuck after various actions (changing track, pattern); CLEAR > UNDO SONG ROW does not work; CLEAR SONG ROW does not clear per-track transpose data; PASTE > UNDO TRANSPOSE does not work; muting a track that another track triggers and unmuting it later leaves the trigs that fell into the muted time muted; muting such a track does not mute its active ARP sequence; the playhead is not shown for the first step triggered by SPP.
stock_bugs.test_tip: POLY-mode and mute behaviour on a modded Monomachine should be compared with stock 1.32B.
stock_bugs.status: open in stock; fixed by a custom firmware
